sentences.zh: 袁洪愈

translations.literal: Yuan Hongyu
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hongyu

sentences.zh: 袁洪愈，字抑之，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Yuan Hongyu, courtesy name Yizhi, was a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hongyu, styled Yizhi, came from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 舉嘉靖二十五年鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing he ranked first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took top honors in the provincial exams in Jiajing 25.

sentences.zh: 明年成進士，授中書舍人。

translations.literal: The following year he passed the palace examination and was appointed Central Secretariat draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became a jinshi and was made a Central Secretariat draftsman.

sentences.zh: 擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to supervising secretary in the Rites section.

sentences.zh: 劾檢討梁紹儒阿附權要，文選郎中白璧招權鬻官，尚書萬鏜、侍郎葛守禮不檢下。

translations.literal: He impeached reviser Liang Shaoru for currying favor with the powerful, Selection Bureau director Bai Bi for abusing power to sell offices, and Ministers Wan Yong and Vice Minister Ge Shouli for failing to restrain subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: He charged reviser Liang Shaoru with fawning on the mighty, Selection Bureau director Bai Bi with trading offices for power, and Ministers Wan Yong and Ge Shouli with lax oversight of their staffs.

sentences.zh: 詔切責鏜、守禮，下璧詔獄，斥紹儒於外。

translations.literal: An edict sternly rebuked Wan Yong and Ge Shouli, sent Bai Bi to the imperial prison, and expelled Liang Shaoru from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sharply rebuked Wan and Ge, imprisoned Bai Bi by edict, and banished Liang Shaoru from court.

sentences.zh: 紹儒，大學士嚴嵩私人也。

translations.literal: Shaoru was a protégé of Grand Secretary Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoru was a private client of Grand Secretary Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 已，陳邊務數事，詔俱從之。

translations.literal: Later he presented several matters concerning border affairs, and the court ordered all to be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted several proposals on frontier affairs, and the court approved them all.

sentences.zh: 嵩屬吏部尚書吳鵬，出為福建僉事。

translations.literal: Song had Minister of Personnel Wu Peng assign him out as Fujian Assistant Administrative Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Song had the Minister of Personnel Wu Peng post him out as Fujian Assistant Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷河南參議、山東提學副使、湖廣參政，所在以清節著。

translations.literal: He served successively as Henan Administrative Commissioner, Shandong Vice Commissioner for Education, and Huguang Administration Commissioner, everywhere noted for incorrupt integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Henan Administrative Commissioner, Shandong Vice Commissioner for Education, and Huguang Administration Commissioner, winning renown everywhere for clean conduct.

sentences.zh: 嵩敗，召為南京太仆少卿，就遷太常。

translations.literal: When Song fell, Hongyu was recalled as Vice Minister of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud, then soon transferred to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Song's downfall he was recalled as Nanjing Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and soon promoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年，以疾歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing he retired owing to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 5 he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，起故官，遷南京工部右侍郎，進右都御史，掌南院事，就改禮部尚書。

translations.literal: During Wanli he was reappointed to his former rank, promoted to Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing, then to Right Censor-in-Chief directing the southern censorate, and then transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli reign he was restored to office, made Nanjing Vice Minister of Works, then Right Censor-in-Chief in charge of the southern censorate, and transferred in place to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 南京御史譚希思疏論中官、外戚，且請循舊制，內閣設絲綸簿，宮門置鐵牌。

translations.literal: Nanjing censor Tan Xisi memorialized concerning eunuchs and maternal relatives, and asked to follow old regulations: the Grand Secretariat should keep a silk-decree register and iron placards should be set at palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing censor Tan Xisi memorialized against eunuchs and consort kin, and asked that old rules be restored: a silk-decree register in the Grand Secretariat and iron placards at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 詔下南京都察院勘訊，將坐以誣罔。

translations.literal: An edict sent the case to the Nanjing Censorate for investigation, intending to convict him of false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the Nanjing Censorate for inquiry, with intent to punish him for calumny.

sentences.zh: 洪愈已改官，代者未至，乃具言希思所陳，載王可大《國憲家猷》、薛應旂《憲章錄》二書。

translations.literal: Hongyu had already changed posts and his successor had not yet arrived; he fully set forth what Xisi had stated, citing Wang Keda's Guoxian Jiayou and Xue Yingqi's Xianzhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyu had already moved to another post and his replacement had not arrived; he therefore laid out Xisi's points in full, citing Wang Keda's Guoxian Jiayou and Xue Yingqi's Xianzhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 帝以所據非頒行制書，謫希思雜職。

translations.literal: The emperor held that the sources cited were not promulgated statutory works and demoted Xisi to a miscellaneous post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that the authorities cited were not officially promulgated statutes and demoted Xisi to a minor post.

sentences.zh: 洪愈尋上疏請禁幹謁，又極諫屯田廢壞之害，乞令商人中鹽，免內地飛挽。

translations.literal: Hongyu soon memorialized to forbid private petitions, and urgently warned of the harm from ruined garrison farms, asking that merchants deliver salt in exchange and that the interior be spared compulsory grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyu soon asked that private solicitations be banned and urgently warned of the ruin of garrison farms, proposing that merchants tender salt in exchange and that forced grain levies in the interior be lifted.

sentences.zh: 皆議行。

translations.literal: All were discussed and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: All were debated and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十五年，就改吏部。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Wanli he was transferred in place to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 15 he was transferred in place to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 其冬引年乞休。

translations.literal: That winter he cited his years and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he pleaded age and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝重其清德，加太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor valued his upright character and granted him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent upon retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor esteemed his integrity and granted him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent on retirement.

sentences.zh: 洪愈通籍四十余年，所居不增一椽，出入徒步。

translations.literal: For more than forty years after entering the registers, Hongyu's dwelling never gained a single rafter; he went out and in on foot.
translations.idiomatic: For more than forty years on the rolls his house never gained a single rafter, and he went everywhere on foot.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 巡撫周孔教捐金葬之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhou Kongjiao contributed funds for his burial.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhou Kongjiao donated money for his burial.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚安節。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Anjie (Peaceful Integrity).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Anjie.

sentences.zh: 子一鶚，以蔭，官治中。

translations.literal: His son Yi E entered office by yin privilege as Court Director.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi E entered office by hereditary privilege as Court Director.

sentences.zh: 饘粥不繼以死。

translations.literal: He died when even thin gruel could not be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: He died when even thin gruel ran out.

sentences.zh: 希思，茶陵人。

translations.literal: Xisi was a native of Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: Xisi was from Chaling.

sentences.zh: 歷右副都御史，巡撫四川。

translations.literal: He rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually became Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 王廷瞻

translations.literal: Wang Tingzhan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingzhan

sentences.zh: 王廷瞻，字稚表，黃岡人。

translations.literal: Wang Tingzhan, courtesy name Zhibiao, was a native of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingzhan, styled Zhibiao, was a native of Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 父濟，參政。

translations.literal: His father Ji was an administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji had been an administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廷瞻舉嘉靖三十八年進士，授淮安推官。

translations.literal: Tingzhan passed the palace examination in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing and was appointed investigating magistrate of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhan became a jinshi in Jiajing 38 and was appointed investigating magistrate of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 入為御史，督畿輔屯政。

translations.literal: He entered service as a censor and supervised garrison-farm policy in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Censorate and oversaw garrison-farm administration in the metropolitan area.

sentences.zh: 穆宗在裕邸，欲易莊田，廷瞻不可。

translations.literal: When the future Muzong was at the Princely Establishment of Yu, he wished to exchange manor lands; Tingzhan refused.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Muzong was still at the Princely Establishment of Yu, he wanted to swap manor lands; Tingzhan would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，所部久雨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing his jurisdiction had long rains.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 his district suffered prolonged rain.

sentences.zh: 請自三宮以下及裕府莊田改入乾清宮者，悉蠲其租。

translations.literal: He asked that rents be remitted on manor lands from the Three Palaces downward and those transferred to the Qianqing Palace from the Princely Establishment of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that rents be remitted on manor lands from the Three Palaces down and on those moved from the Princely Establishment of Yu into the Qianqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 詔減十之五。

translations.literal: An edict reduced them by half.
translations.idiomatic: An edict cut the rents by half.

sentences.zh: 已，言勛戚莊田太濫，請於初給時裁量田數，限其世次，爵絕歸官。

translations.literal: Later he said that estates granted to meritorious officials and consort kin were too lavish, and asked that at the initial grant the acreage be measured, the number of generations limited, and when the title lapsed the land revert to the state.
translations.idiomatic: He later argued that estates for meritorious kin and consort families were excessive, and proposed that at the first grant the fields be measured, succession limited by generation, and the land revert to the state when the title expired.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The measure was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 高拱再輔政，廷瞻常論拱，遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: When Gao Gong again served as chief minister, Tingzhan often criticized him and therefore resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Gong returned as chief minister, Tingzhan repeatedly attacked him and finally retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，起故官。

translations.literal: When Shenzong took the throne, Tingzhan was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Tingzhan was recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 歷太仆卿。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年，以右僉都御史巡撫四川。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 番屢犯松潘。

translations.literal: Tribes repeatedly raided Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian bands repeatedly attacked Songpan.

sentences.zh: 廷瞻令副使楊一桂、總兵官劉顯剿之，殲其魁，群蠻納款。

translations.literal: Tingzhan had Vice Commissioner Yang Yigui and Regional Commander Liu Xian suppress them, destroying their leaders; the tribes submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhan ordered Vice Commissioner Yang Yigui and Regional Commander Liu Xian to campaign against them, wiped out their chiefs, and the tribes surrendered.

sentences.zh: 風村、白草諸番，久居二十八砦，率男婦八千余人來降。

translations.literal: The Fengcun and Baicao tribes, long entrenched in twenty-eight stockades, came in with more than eight thousand men, women, and children.
translations.idiomatic: The Fengcun and Baicao tribes, long holding twenty-eight stockades, brought in more than eight thousand men, women, and children to submit.

sentences.zh: 復命總兵顯討建昌、傀廈、洗馬、姑宰、鐵口諸叛番，皆獻首惡出降。

translations.literal: He again ordered Regional Commander Xian to attack the rebel tribes of Jianchang, Kuixia, Xima, Guzai, and Tiekou; all presented the ringleaders and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He again ordered Commander Xian to subdue the rebel tribes of Jianchang, Kuixia, Xima, Guzai, and Tiekou; each turned over its chief culprits and submitted.

sentences.zh: 增俸一級，進右副都御史，撫南、贛。

translations.literal: His salary grade was raised one step; he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: His salary grade rose one step; he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Nan and Gan.

sentences.zh: 入為南京大理卿。

translations.literal: He entered service as Nanjing Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Nanjing Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 歷兩京戶部左、右侍郎，以右都御史出督漕運兼巡撫鳳陽諸府。

translations.literal: He served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Revenue in both capitals, then went out as Right Censor-in-Chief to supervise grain transport and grand coordinate Fengyang and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Revenue in both capitals, then went out as Right Censor-in-Chief to supervise the grain transport and grand coordinate Fengyang and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 寶應氾光湖堤蓄水濟運，平江伯陳瑄所築也。

translations.literal: The Baoying embankment on Lake Fan stored water to aid transport; it had been built by the Marquis of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Baoying embankment on Lake Fan impounded water for the transport canals; it had been built by the Marquis of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan.

sentences.zh: 下流無所泄，決為八淺，匯成巨潭，諸鹽場皆沒。

translations.literal: With no outlet below, it burst into eight shallows and formed a vast pool; all the salt fields were submerged.
translations.idiomatic: With no outlet downstream it broke into eight shallows and formed a great lagoon, drowning the salt works.

sentences.zh: 淮流復奔入，勢益氵匈氵勇前巡撫李世達等議開越河避其險，廷瞻承之。

translations.literal: The Huai River again poured in and the current grew ever more turbulent. Former Grand Coordinator Li Shidao and others had proposed opening the Yue River to avoid the danger; Tingzhan carried the plan forward.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai again rushed in and the current grew fiercer still. Former Grand Coordinator Li Shidao and others had proposed cutting the Yue River to skirt the hazard; Tingzhan took up the project.

sentences.zh: 鑿渠千七百七十六丈，為石閘三，減水閘二，石堤三千三十六丈，子堤五千三百九十丈，費公帑二十余萬，八月竣事。

translations.literal: They dug a channel 1,776 zhang long, built three stone sluices, two flood sluices, 3,036 zhang of stone embankment and 5,390 zhang of secondary embankment, spending more than 200,000 taels of public funds; the work was finished in eight months.
translations.idiomatic: They excavated a channel 1,776 zhang long, erected three stone sluices and two flood sluices, laid 3,036 zhang of stone dike and 5,390 zhang of subsidiary dike, at a cost of more than 200,000 taels of public money, and finished in eight months.

sentences.zh: 詔旨褒嘉，賜河名弘濟。

translations.literal: An edict praised the achievement and bestowed on the canal the name Hongji (Great Relief).
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended the work and named the canal Hongji.

sentences.zh: 進廷瞻戶部尚書，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: Tingzhan was promoted to Minister of Revenue while remaining grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhan was promoted to Minister of Revenue while continuing as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 尋改南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Nanjing Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Nanjing Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 未上，乞歸。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Before assuming the post he asked to go home.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long interval he died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 兄廷陳，見《文苑傳》。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tingchen is treated in the "Writers" biography.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Tingchen is treated in the Writers biography.

sentences.zh: 郭應聘

translations.literal: Guo Yingpin
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yingpin

sentences.zh: 郭應聘，字君賓，莆田人。

translations.literal: Guo Yingpin, courtesy name Junbin, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yingpin, styled Junbin, was from Putian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the palace examination in the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Jiajing 29.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 歷郎中，出為南寧知府。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to bureau director, then went out as prefect of Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to bureau director, then went out as prefect of Nanning.

sentences.zh: 遷威茂兵備副使，轉廣東參政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner for Weimao defense, then to Guangdong Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Commissioner for Weimao defense, then Guangdong Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從提督吳桂芳平李亞元，別擊賊首張韶南、黃仕良等。

translations.literal: Following Grand Coordinator Wu Guifang he pacified Li Yayuan, and separately attacked the bandit chiefs Zhang Shaonan and Huang Shiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Following Grand Coordinator Wu Guifang he pacified Li Yayuan and separately struck the bandit chiefs Zhang Shaonan and Huang Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 遷廣西按察使，歷左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He was made Guangxi Surveillance Commissioner, then served as Left and Right Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Guangxi Surveillance Commissioner and later Left and Right Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年大破古田賊，斬獲七千有奇。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing he inflicted a great defeat on the Gutian bandits, beheading or capturing more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 4 he routed the Gutian bandits, killing or capturing more than seven thousand.

sentences.zh: 已，從巡撫殷正茂平古田，再進秩。

translations.literal: Later, following Grand Coordinator Yin Zhengmao, he pacified Gutian again and was promoted once more.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Grand Coordinator Yin Zhengmao, he pacified Gutian again and received another promotion.

sentences.zh: 正茂遷總督，遂擢應聘右副都御史代之。

translations.literal: When Zhengmao was transferred to governor-general, Yingpin was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengmao became governor-general, Yingpin was raised to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 府江瑤反。

translations.literal: The Yao of Fujiang rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao of Fujiang rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 府江上起陽朔，下達昭平，亙三百餘里。

translations.literal: Fujiang runs from Yangshuo down to Zhaoping, more than three hundred li in length.
translations.idiomatic: Fujiang stretches from Yangshuo to Zhaoping, more than three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 諸瑤夾江居，怙險剽劫。

translations.literal: The Yao lived on both banks, relying on the terrain to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yao communities lined both banks, trusting the narrows to raid and rob.

sentences.zh: 成化、正德間，都御史韓雍、陳金討平之，至是攻圍荔浦、永安，劫知州楊惟執、指揮胡翰。

translations.literal: During the Chenghua and Zhengde reigns, Censors-in-Chief Han Yong and Chen Jin had pacified them; now they besieged Lipu and Yong'an and seized Prefect Yang Weizhi and Commander Hu Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chenghua and Zhengde periods Han Yong and Chen Jin as censors-in-chief had suppressed them; now the Yao attacked Lipu and Yong'an and took Prefect Yang Weizhi and Commander Hu Han captive.

sentences.zh: 事聞，大學士張居正奏假便宜，寓書應聘曰：「炎荒瘴癘區，役數萬眾，不宜淹留，速破其巢，則余賊破膽。」

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng memorialized for discretionary authority and wrote to Yingpin: "This is a malarial frontier; to keep tens of thousands of troops there long is unwise. Break their nests quickly and the rest will lose heart."
translations.idiomatic: On report, Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng asked leave to act at discretion and wrote Yingpin: "In that feverish frontier you should not detain tens of thousands of men; smash their lairs at once and the rest will lose heart."

sentences.zh: 應聘集土、漢兵六萬，令總兵官李錫進討。

translations.literal: Yingpin assembled sixty thousand native and Han troops and ordered Regional Commander Li Xi to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yingpin mustered sixty thousand native and Han soldiers and ordered Regional Commander Li Xi to campaign.

sentences.zh: 未行，而懷遠瑤亦殺知縣馬希武反。

translations.literal: Before they marched, the Yao of Huaiyuan also killed Prefect Ma Xiwu and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before the column moved, the Huaiyuan Yao killed Prefect Ma Xiwu and rose.

sentences.zh: 應聘與正茂議先征府江，三閱月悉定，乃檄錫討懷遠。

translations.literal: Yingpin and Zhengmao agreed to strike Fujiang first; in three months all was settled, then he ordered Xi to attack Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yingpin and Zhengmao decided to pacify Fujiang first; within three months it was quiet, and he then dispatched Xi against Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 天大雨雪，無功而還。

translations.literal: Heavy rain and snow fell; they achieved nothing and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Great rains and snow came; the army accomplished nothing and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 懷遠，古牂牁，地界湖、貴靖、黎諸州，環郭皆瑤，編氓處其外。

translations.literal: Huaiyuan, ancient Zangge, bordered the prefectures of Huguang, Guizhou, Jing, and Li; Yao surrounded the walled city while registered subjects lived outside.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyuan, the old Zangge country, lay among Huguang, Guizhou, Jing, and Li; Yao ringed the seat while registered households lived beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，征之不克，知縣寄居府城，遙示羈縻而已。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign campaigns failed to subdue it; the prefect resided in the superior prefecture and exercised distant suzerainty only.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing campaigns had failed; the prefect lodged in the superior city and ruled only by loose rein.

sentences.zh: 古田既復，瑤懾兵威，願服屬，希武始入其地。

translations.literal: After Gutian was recovered the Yao feared the army and wished to submit; only then did Xiwu enter their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gutian was retaken the Yao feared the troops and offered allegiance; Xiwu then entered the district.

sentences.zh: 議築城，董作過峻，瑤遂亂，希武見殺。

translations.literal: When a city was proposed the corvée was too harsh and the Yao rebelled; Xiwu was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Plans for a walled city pressed labor too hard; the Yao revolted and Xiwu was slain.

sentences.zh: 及是，師出無功。

translations.literal: Thus this expedition gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: That campaign therefore ended without success.

sentences.zh: 應聘益調諸路兵，鎮撫白杲、黃土、大梅、青淇侗、僮，以孤賊勢，而錫與諸將連破賊，斬其魁，懷遠乃下。

translations.literal: Yingpin then mobilized troops from every circuit, had pacification commissioners win over the Dong and Zhuang of Baiguo, Huangtu, Damei, and Qingqi, to isolate the rebels, while Xi and the generals broke them in succession, beheaded their chiefs, and Huaiyuan submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yingpin called up forces from all routes, won over the Dong and Zhuang of Baiguo, Huangtu, Damei, and Qingqi to cut the rebels off, and Xi with the generals smashed them in turn, slew their leaders, and Huaiyuan fell.

sentences.zh: 事皆具錫傳。

translations.literal: The details are given in Xi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in Xi's biography.

sentences.zh: 初議行師，錫以陽朔金寶嶺賊近，欲先滅之。

translations.literal: When the campaign was first planned, Xi wanted to destroy the bandits at Jinbaoling near Yangshuo first.
translations.idiomatic: At the first planning, Xi wished to wipe out the Yangshuo Jinbaoling bandits first.

sentences.zh: 應聘曰：「君第往，吾自有處。」

translations.literal: Yingpin said: "You go on; I shall handle it myself."
translations.idiomatic: Yingpin said: "March on; I have my own plan."

sentences.zh: 錫行數日，應聘與按察使吳一介出不意襲殺其魁。

translations.literal: After Xi had marched several days, Yingpin with Surveillance Commissioner Wu Yijie surprised and killed their chief.
translations.idiomatic: A few days after Xi left, Yingpin with Surveillance Commissioner Wu Yijie surprised and slew the chief.

sentences.zh: 比懷遠克復，陽朔亦定，乃分遣諸將門崇文、楊照、亦孔昭等討洛容、上油、邊山。

translations.literal: When Huaiyuan was recovered and Yangshuo was quiet, he sent Generals Men Chongwen, Yang Zhao, and Yi Kongzhao to subdue Luorong, Shangyou, and Bianshan.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaiyuan and Yangshuo were settled he sent Generals Men Chongwen, Yang Zhao, and Yi Kongzhao against Luorong, Shangyou, and Bianshan.

sentences.zh: 五叛瑤悉平。

translations.literal: The five rebel Yao groups were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All five rebel Yao bands were pacified.

sentences.zh: 神宗大悅，進兵部右侍郎兼右副都御史，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: Shenzong was greatly pleased and promoted him to Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, retaining his grand coordinator post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and made him Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief while he remained grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年，召為戶部右侍郎，尋以憂歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli he was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue, but soon retired on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 2 he was called to be Vice Minister of Revenue, then soon left on mourning.

sentences.zh: 八年起，改兵部，兼右僉都御史，仍撫廣西。

translations.literal: Recalled in the eighth year, he was transferred to the Ministry of War with concurrent Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and still grand coordinated Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled in year 8, he was moved to War with concurrent Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and still governed Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時十寨初下，應聘與總督劉堯誨奏設三鎮，隸賓州，以土巡檢守之，而統於思恩參將，十寨遂安。

translations.literal: When the Ten Stockades had just submitted, Yingpin with Governor-General Liu Yaohui memorialized to establish three garrisons under Binzhou, guarded by native inspecting officers under the Sinan regional commander, and the Ten Stockades were thereafter secure.
translations.idiomatic: With the Ten Stockades newly pacified, he and Governor-General Liu Yaohui asked three garrisons under Binzhou, native inspecting officers, and the Sinan regional commander; the stockades then stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 進右都御史兼兵部右侍郎，總督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War, governor-general of the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War, governor-general of both Guang.

sentences.zh: 前總督多受將吏金，應聘悉謝絕。

translations.literal: Former governors-general had often taken gold from officers; Yingpin refused it all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier governors-general had taken officers' gold; Yingpin refused every gift.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召掌南京都察院，以吳文華代。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned to head the Nanjing Censorate, with Wu Wenhua replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was called to head the Nanjing Censorate; Wu Wenhua replaced him.

sentences.zh: 頃之，就拜兵部尚書，參贊機務。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of War with concurrent participation in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of War with a seat in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 久之，引疾歸。

translations.literal: After a long time he retired citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 應聘在廣西，奏復陳獻章、王守仁祠。

translations.literal: While in Guangxi he memorialized to restore the shrines of Chen Xianzhang and Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxi he asked to restore the shrines of Chen Xianzhang and Wang Shouren.

sentences.zh: 劉臺謫戍潯州，為僦居供廩，歿復賻斂歸其喪，像祀之。

translations.literal: Liu Tai, banished to Xunzhou, he rented lodging for and supplied rations; when Liu died he paid for the funeral and sent the body home and enshrined his image.
translations.idiomatic: For Liu Tai, exiled to Xunzhou, he rented quarters and supplied grain; when Liu died he paid the funeral costs, sent the body home, and set up his portrait for worship.

sentences.zh: 官南京，與海瑞敦儉素，士大夫不敢侈汰。

translations.literal: At Nanjing he and Hai Rui practiced frugality so that scholar-officials dared not live lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanjing he and Hai Rui lived plainly, and gentlemen dared not be extravagant.

sentences.zh: 歸七月卒。

translations.literal: Seven months after returning home he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died seven months after going home.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚襄靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Xiangjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Xiangjing.

sentences.zh: 吳文華，字子彬，連江人。

translations.literal: Wu Wenhua, courtesy name Zibin, was a native of Lianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wenhua, styled Zibin, was from Lianjiang.

sentences.zh: 父世澤，府江兵備副使，有威名。

translations.literal: His father Shize had been Vice Commissioner for Fujiang defense and enjoyed a formidable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shize, Fujiang defense vice commissioner, had a stern name.

sentences.zh: 文華舉嘉靖三十五年進士，授南京兵部主事。

translations.literal: Wenhua passed the palace examination in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing and was appointed principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua became a jinshi in Jiajing 35 and was made principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 歷四川右參政，與平土官鳳繼祖。

translations.literal: He served as Sichuan Right Administration Commissioner and helped pacify the native official Feng Jizu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Sichuan Right Administration Commissioner and helped pacify the native official Feng Jizu.

sentences.zh: 四遷河南左布政使。

translations.literal: After four promotions he became Henan Left Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions he became Henan Left Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年，以右副都御史巡撫廣西。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 3 he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 討平南鄉、陸平、周塘、板寨瑤及昭平黎福莊父子。

translations.literal: He suppressed the Yao of Nanxiang, Luping, Zhoutang, and Banzhai and the father and son Li Fuzhuang of Zhaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the Yao of Nanxiang, Luping, Zhoutang, and Banzhai and the Li Fuzhuang father and son of Zhaoping.

sentences.zh: 偕總督淩雲翼征河池、咘咳、北三瑤。

translations.literal: With Governor-General Ling Yunyi he campaigned against the Hechi, Buqi, and Northern Three Yao.
translations.idiomatic: With Governor-General Ling Yunyi he campaigned against the Hechi, Buqi, and Northern Three Yao.

sentences.zh: 三瑤未為逆，雲翼喜事，殺戮甚慘，得蔭襲，文華亦受賞。

translations.literal: The Three Yao had not rebelled, but Yunyi loved action and slaughtered cruelly; he gained a hereditary privilege and Wenhua also received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Yao were not in revolt, yet Yunyi, eager for action, killed savagely; he won a hereditary privilege and Wenhua shared the reward.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部右侍郎，請終養歸。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, he asked to retire and care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Made Vice Minister of Revenue, he asked leave to nurse his parents.

sentences.zh: 起兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，仍撫廣西。

translations.literal: He was raised to Vice Minister of War with concurrent Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and still grand coordinated Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Vice Minister of War with concurrent Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and still governed Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 遷總督兩廣軍務，巡撫廣東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor-general of the two Guang military affairs and Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He became governor-general of the two Guang and Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 進右都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 會巡撫吳善、總兵呼良朋討平嚴秀珠。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Grand Coordinators Wu Shan and Regional Commander Hu Liangpeng had pacified Yan Xiuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Coordinators Wu Shan and Commander Hu Liangpeng had pacified Yan Xiuzhu.

sentences.zh: 岑崗賊李珍、江月照拒命久，文華購擒月照，平珍。

translations.literal: The Cengang bandits Li Zhen and Jiang Yuezhao had long defied orders; Wenhua bought Yuezhao's capture and pacified Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The Cengang rebels Li Zhen and Jiang Yuezhao had long resisted; Wenhua bought Yuezhao's capture and settled Zhen.

sentences.zh: 尋入為南京工部尚書，就改兵部。

translations.literal: Soon he entered service as Nanjing Minister of Works and was then transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered as Nanjing Minister of Works and was moved to War.

sentences.zh: 引疾去。

translations.literal: He resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 仍起南京工部，力辭，虛位三年以待。

translations.literal: He was again offered Nanjing Works but firmly declined; the post waited empty three years for him.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Works was offered again; he firmly refused, and the seat stood empty three years awaiting him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚襄惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Xianghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Xianghui.

sentences.zh: 耿定向

translations.literal: Geng Dingxiang
translations.idiomatic: Geng Dingxiang

sentences.zh: 耿定向，字在倫，黃安人。

translations.literal: Geng Dingxiang, courtesy name Zailun, was a native of Huang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Dingxiang, styled Zailun, was from Huang'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the palace examination in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Jiajing 35.

sentences.zh: 除行人，擢御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier and then promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a courier, then raised to censor.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩父子竊政，吏部尚書吳鵬附之。

translations.literal: Yan Song and his son usurped power; Minister of Personnel Wu Peng attached himself to them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song father and son held power; Minister Wu Peng clung to them.

sentences.zh: 定向疏鵬六罪，因言鵬婿學士董份總裁會試，私鵬子紹，宜並斥。

translations.literal: Dingxiang memorialized six crimes of Peng and, because Academician Dong Fen oversaw the metropolitan examination and favored Peng's son Shao, asked that Fen also be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxiang listed six crimes of Peng and, since Academician Dong Fen ran the metropolitan exams and favored Peng's son Shao, asked that Fen be expelled too.

sentences.zh: 嵩為營護，事竟寢。

translations.literal: Song intervened to protect them and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Song shielded them and the case died.

sentences.zh: 出按甘肅，舉劾無所私。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect Gansu, he promoted and demoted without favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: As touring censor in Gansu he promoted and punished without partiality.

sentences.zh: 去任，行笥一肩。

translations.literal: When he left office his traveling chest was a single shoulder pole.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving, his traveling chest was one shoulder pole.

sentences.zh: 有以石經饋者，留境上而去。

translations.literal: Someone presented a stone classic and left it on the border as he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone offered a stone classic; he left it on the border and went on.

sentences.zh: 還督南京學政。

translations.literal: On return he supervised Nanjing educational administration.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he oversaw Nanjing education.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，擢大理右寺丞。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing he was promoted to Right Assistant in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing he was made Right Assistant in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 高拱執政，定向嘗譏其褊淺無大臣度，拱嗛之。

translations.literal: When Gao Gong held power, Dingxiang had mocked his narrowness and lack of ministerial breadth; Gong resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong in power had been mocked by Dingxiang for pettiness unworthy of a chief minister; Gong bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及拱掌吏部，以考察謫定向橫州判官。

translations.literal: When Gong took the Ministry of Personnel he used the performance review to demote Dingxiang to magistrate of Hengzhou in Heng.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong ran Personnel he used the review to demote Dingxiang to magistrate of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 拱罷，量移衡州推官。

translations.literal: After Gong fell he was transferred in grade to investigating magistrate of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Gong fell he was moved in grade to investigating magistrate of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，累官右副都御史。

translations.literal: During Wanli he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎陸光祖為御史周之翰所劾，光祖已留，定向復頌光祖賢，詆之翰。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Lu Guangzu was impeached by Censor Zhou Zhihan; Guangzu had already been retained when Dingxiang again praised Guangzu and denounced Zhihan.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Lu Guangzu was impeached by Censor Zhou Zhihan; Lu was kept on, but Dingxiang praised Lu and attacked Zhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中李以謙言定向擠言官，定向求去，帝不問。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Li Yiqian said Dingxiang was squeezing out remonstrators; Dingxiang asked to leave and the emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Yiqian said Dingxiang was driving out critics; Dingxiang asked to quit and the emperor did not pursue it.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部左、右侍郎，擢南京右都御史。

translations.literal: He served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Punishments and was promoted to Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Punishments and was made Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 御史王藩臣劾應天巡撫周繼，疏發逾月不以白定向。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Fanchen impeached Grand Coordinator Zhou Ji of Yingtian, but more than a month passed before the memorial was reported to Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Fanchen impeached Yingtian Coordinator Zhou Ji, yet the memorial reached Dingxiang only after more than a month.

sentences.zh: 定向怒，守故事力爭，自劾求罷，且詆藩臣論劾失當。

translations.literal: Dingxiang was angry, insisted on precedent, submitted his own resignation, and also attacked Fanchen for improper impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxiang was furious, clung to precedent, resigned in protest, and also denounced Fanchen's impeachment as improper.

sentences.zh: 因言故江西巡撫陳有年、四川巡撫徐元泰皆賢，為御史方萬山、王麟趾劾罷，今宜召用，而量罰藩臣。

translations.literal: He said former Jiangxi Coordinator Chen Younian and Sichuan Coordinator Xu Yuantai were both worthy but had been driven out by Censors Fang Wanshan and Wang Linzhi, who should now be recalled while Fanchen was punished in measure.
translations.idiomatic: He said Coordinators Chen Younian of Jiangxi and Xu Yuantai of Sichuan were worthy men ousted by Fang Wanshan and Wang Linzhi, who should be recalled while Fanchen was punished proportionately.

sentences.zh: 藩臣坐停俸二月。

translations.literal: Fanchen was fined two months' salary.
translations.idiomatic: Fanchen was fined two months' salary.

sentences.zh: 於是給事中許弘綱、觀政進士薛敷教、南京御史黃仁榮及麟趾連章劾定向。

translations.literal: Then Supervising Secretary Xu Honggang, observing student Xue Fujiao, Nanjing Censor Huang Renrong, and Linzhi all memorialized against Dingxiang in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Then Supervising Secretary Xu Honggang, student Xue Fujiao, Nanjing Censor Huang Renrong, and Linzhi impeached Dingxiang in turn.

sentences.zh: 麟趾言：「南臺去京師遠，章疏先傳，人得為計。

translations.literal: Linzhi said: "The southern censorate is far from the capital; memorials are transmitted first and people can scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Linzhi said: "The southern board is far from court; memorials travel ahead and men can plot.

sentences.zh: 如御史孫鳴治論魏國公徐邦瑞，陳揚善論主事劉以煥，皆因奏辭豫聞，一則夤緣幸免，一則捃摭被誣。

translations.literal: When Censor Sun Mingzhi impeached Regional Commander Xu Bangrui of Wei and Chen Yangshan impeached Director Liu Yihuan, both learned of the charges beforehand—one escaped by pull, the other was framed by gathered faults.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Sun Mingzhi attacked Wei Regional Commander Xu Bangrui and Chen Yangshan attacked Director Liu Yihuan, both learned early—one escaped by favor, the other was trapped by piled charges.

sentences.zh: 故邇來投揭有遲浹月者，事理宜然，非自藩臣始。」

translations.literal: Thus recent petitions sometimes arrive a month late; that is how things work and did not begin with Fanchen."
translations.idiomatic: Hence recent submissions sometimes lag a month; that is natural and did not start with Fanchen."

sentences.zh: 語並侵大學士許國、左都御史吳時來、副都御史詹仰庇。

translations.literal: His words also impugned Grand Secretaries Xu Guo, Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhan Yangbi.
translations.idiomatic: He also struck at Grand Secretaries Xu Guo, Left Censor Wu Shilai, and Vice Censor Zhan Yangbi.

sentences.zh: 執政方惡言者，勒敷教還籍省過，麟趾、仁榮亦停俸。

translations.literal: The ruling faction hated critics; Fujiao was sent home to reflect, and Linzhi and Renrong also had salaries stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers hated outspoken men; Fujiao was sent home to repent, and Linzhi and Renrong lost salary.

sentences.zh: 時已除定向戶部尚書督倉場，定向因力辭求退。

translations.literal: Dingxiang had already been appointed Minister of Revenue to supervise the granaries; he therefore repeatedly asked to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxiang had been named Minister of Revenue over the granaries; he pressed hard to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 章屢上，乃許。

translations.literal: After many memorials permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated memorials he was allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚恭簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Gongjian.

sentences.zh: 定向初立朝有時望。

translations.literal: Dingxiang at first had standing when he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxiang at first had repute at court.

sentences.zh: 後歷徐階、張居正、申時行、王錫爵四輔，皆能無齟齬。

translations.literal: Later he served under four chief ministers—Xu Jie, Zhang Juzheng, Shen Shixing, and Wang Xijue—and was able to avoid friction with all.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served four chief ministers—Xu Jie, Zhang Juzheng, Shen Shixing, and Wang Xijue—without friction.

sentences.zh: 至居正奪情，寓書友人譽為伊尹而貶言者，時議訾之。

translations.literal: When Juzheng seized mourning leave he wrote friends praising him as an Yi Yin and belittling critics; opinion condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng took mourning leave he wrote friends calling him an Yi Yin and mocking critics; opinion blamed him.

sentences.zh: 其學本王守仁。

translations.literal: His learning derived from Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: His doctrine came from Wang Shouren.

sentences.zh: 嘗招晉江李贄於黃安，後漸惡之，贄亦屢短定向。

translations.literal: He once invited Li Zhi of Jinjiang to Huang'an; later he came to dislike him, and Zhi also often disparaged Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He once invited Li Zhi of Jinjiang to Huang'an; later they grew hostile and Zhi often slighted him.

sentences.zh: 士大夫好禪者往往從贄遊。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials fond of Chan often followed Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen enamored of Chan often followed Zhi.

sentences.zh: 贄小有才，機辨，定向不能勝也。

translations.literal: Zhi had minor talent and was quick-witted; Dingxiang could not best him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had small talent and sharp tongue; Dingxiang could not overcome him.

sentences.zh: 贄為姚安知府，一旦自去其發，冠服坐堂皇，上官勒令解任。

translations.literal: Zhi was prefect of Yao'an; one day he shaved his head, donned monastic garb, and sat in the hall; his superiors forced him to resign.
translations.idiomatic: As Yao'an prefect Zhi one day shaved his head, put on monk's dress, and sat in the hall; superiors made him quit.

sentences.zh: 居黃安，日引士人講學，雜以婦女，專崇釋氏，卑侮孔、孟。

translations.literal: Living at Huang'an he daily gathered gentlemen to lecture, mixed in women, exalted Buddhism alone, and belittled Confucius and Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: At Huang'an he lectured daily, admitted women, exalted Buddhism, and scorned Confucius and Mencius.

sentences.zh: 後北遊通州，為給事中張問達所劾，逮死獄中。

translations.literal: Later he traveled north to Tongzhou and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhang Wenda; he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went north to Tongzhou; Supervising Secretary Zhang Wenda impeached him and he died in jail.

sentences.zh: 定向弟定理、定力。

translations.literal: Dingxiang's younger brothers Dingli and Dingli.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were Dingli and Dingli.

sentences.zh: 定理終諸生。

translations.literal: Dingli ended as a student of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Dingli remained a National University student.

sentences.zh: 與定向俱講學，專主禪機。

translations.literal: With Dingxiang he lectured together, specializing in Chan subtleties.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured with Dingxiang, devoted to Chan mysteries.

sentences.zh: 定力，隆慶中進士，除工部主事。

translations.literal: Dingli passed the palace examination in Longqing and was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Dingli became a jinshi in Longqing and was made principal clerk in Works.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，累官右僉都御史，督操江，疏陳礦使之患。

translations.literal: During Wanli he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, supervised the Yangtze patrol, and memorialized on the harm of mining envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, commanded the Yangtze patrol, and warned of mining commissioners.

sentences.zh: 再遷南京兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Again he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Right Vice Minister of War in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was conferred the rank of Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was posthumously made a full minister.

sentences.zh: 王樵，字明遠，金壇人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiao, styled Mingyuan, was a native of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiao, courtesy name Mingyuan, came from Jintan.

sentences.zh: 父臬，兵部主事。

translations.literal: His father Nie was a principal clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nie served as principal clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 諫武宗南巡，被杖。

translations.literal: He remonstrated against Emperor Wuzong's southern tour and was beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke out against the Wuzong emperor's southern tour and was flogged at court.

sentences.zh: 終山東副使。

translations.literal: He ended as vice commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Shandong vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 樵舉嘉靖二十六年進士，授行人。

translations.literal: Qiao passed the palace examination in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing and was appointed emissary.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao became a jinshi in Jiajing 26 and was made an emissary in the Hanlin service.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as assistant department director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to assistant director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 著《讀律私箋》，甚精核。

translations.literal: He authored "Private Notes on Reading the Penal Code," which was very precise and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Du Lu Si Jian, a work noted for its precise and rigorous legal analysis.

sentences.zh: 胡宗憲計降汪直，欲赦直以示信。

translations.literal: Hu Zongxian plotted to induce Wang Zhi to surrender and wished to pardon Zhi to show good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongxian sought Wang Zhi's surrender and wanted to grant him amnesty as a sign of sincerity.

sentences.zh: 樵言此叛民與他納降異，直遂誅。

translations.literal: Qiao said this rebel people differed from others who submitted in surrender; Zhi was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao argued that this rebel was unlike ordinary capitulators; Wang Zhi was executed as a result.

sentences.zh: 遷山東僉事，移疾歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shandong assistant commissioner and returned home citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Shandong assistant commissioner, he soon retired claiming illness.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，張居正柄國，雅知樵，起補浙江僉事，擢尚寶卿。

translations.literal: Early in Wanli, Zhang Juzheng held state power; having long known Qiao, he recalled him to fill Zhejiang assistant commissioner and promoted him to Director of the Directorate of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wanli reign Zhang Juzheng, who knew Qiao well, recalled him as Zhejiang assistant commissioner and then promoted him to Director of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 劉臺劾居正，居正乞歸。

translations.literal: Liu Tai impeached Juzheng; Juzheng begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tai impeached Zhang Juzheng, who then asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 諸曹奏留之，樵獨請全諫臣以安大臣，略言：「自古明主欲開言路，言不當，猶優容之；

translations.literal: The various offices memorialized to retain him; Qiao alone asked to protect remonstrating officials to reassure senior ministers, stating in brief: "Since ancient times enlightened rulers wishing to open the path of speech, even when words were improper, still treated speakers with forbearance;
translations.idiomatic: Offices urged Zhang to stay; Qiao alone pleaded to shield critics and reassure the chief minister, writing in part: "Enlightened rulers have always kept counsel open—even mistaken speech they still tolerated;

sentences.zh: 大臣欲廣上德，人攻己，猶薦拔之。

translations.literal: Senior ministers wishing to extend the ruler's virtue, when people attacked themselves, still recommended and promoted them.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers who sought to magnify their lord's virtue would promote those who criticized them.

sentences.zh: 如宋文彥博於唐介是也。

translations.literal: Such as Wen Yanbo of Song toward Tang Jie was the case.
translations.idiomatic: This was like Wen Yanbo of Song toward Tang Jie.

sentences.zh: 今居正留而臺得罪，無乃非仁宗待唐介意乎！」

translations.literal: Now Juzheng stays while Tai is punished—might this not fail to match how Emperor Renzong treated Tang Jie!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Juzheng remains while Liu Tai is punished—is this not far from how Emperor Renzong treated Tang Jie?"

sentences.zh: 居正大恚，出為南京鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Juzheng was greatly incensed and transferred him out as Director of Ceremonies in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was furious and had him posted to Nanjing as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 旋因星變自陳，罷之。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of a celestial omen, he memorialized on his own conduct, and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he offered his resignation after a portent in the heavens and was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 家居十余年，起南京太仆少卿，時年七十余矣。

translations.literal: He lived at home more than ten years; then he was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing—by then he was over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a decade at home he was recalled as Nanjing vice director of the Imperial Stud, already in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 歲中再遷大理卿，尋拜南京刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Within the year he was transferred again to Director of Punishments, and soon appointed Right Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he rose again to chief of the Court of Judicial Review, then became Right Vice Minister of Justice in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 誠意伯劉世延主使殺人，樵當世延革任。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Chengyi, Liu Shiyan, masterminded a murder; Qiao ruled that Shiyan be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Chengyi Liu Shiyan was found to have ordered a killing, Qiao ruled to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 尋就擢右都御史。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 給事中盧大中劾其衰老，帝令致仕。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Lu Dazhong impeached him for senility; the emperor ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Lu Dazhong attacked him as too old; the emperor told him to retire.

sentences.zh: 樵恬淡誠愨，溫然長者。

translations.literal: Qiao was placid, sincere, and guileless—a warm elder in manner.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was calm, honest, and unassuming—a gentle elder in bearing.

sentences.zh: 邃經學，《易》、《書》、《春秋》皆有纂述。

translations.literal: He was deeply versed in classical learning and had compiled works on the Changes, Documents, and Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply learned in the classics, he produced writings on the Changes, Documents, and Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保，謚恭簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was conferred Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Gongjian ("Respectful and Plain").

sentences.zh: 子肯堂，字宇泰。

translations.literal: His son Kentang, styled Yutai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kentang, courtesy name Yutai.

sentences.zh: 舉萬曆十七年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He passed the palace examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Wanli 17, entered the Hanlin as bachelor, and was made reviser.

sentences.zh: 倭寇朝鮮，疏陳十議，願假御史銜練兵海上。

translations.literal: When Wokou raided Korea, he memorialized ten proposals and wished to borrow censor rank to train troops on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates struck Korea he laid out ten proposals and asked to drill troops at sea with censorial rank.

sentences.zh: 疏留中，因引疾歸。

translations.literal: The memorial was kept within the palace; he therefore cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was shelved; he retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 京察，降調。

translations.literal: At the capital evaluation he was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: At the metropolitan review he was demoted and reassigned.

sentences.zh: 家居久之，吏部侍郎楊時喬薦補南京行人司副。

translations.literal: After long residence at home, Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Shiqiao recommended him to fill Deputy Director of the Nanjing Directorate of Royal Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: After years at home Yang Shiqiao, vice minister of Personnel, recommended him as deputy director of Royal Carriages in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 終福建參政。

translations.literal: He ended as administration commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Fujian administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 肯堂好讀書，尤精於醫，所著《證治準繩》該博精粹，世競傳之。

translations.literal: Kentang loved reading and was especially skilled in medicine; his work "Standards of Pattern Identification and Treatment" was comprehensive and refined, and the world eagerly circulated it.
translations.idiomatic: Kentang loved books and excelled in medicine; his Zheng Zhi Zhun Sheng was encyclopedic and precise, and widely copied.

sentences.zh: 魏時亮

translations.literal: Wei Shiliang.
translations.idiomatic: The biographical subject is Wei Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 魏時亮，字工甫，南昌人。

translations.literal: Wei Shiliang, styled Gongfu, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shiliang, courtesy name Gongfu, came from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the palace examination in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Jiajing 38.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人，擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary in the Secretariat Directorate and promoted to supervising secretary of the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a secretariat secretary and then promoted to supervising secretary in the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年正月七日，有詔免朝，越三日，復傳免。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the first month of the first year of Longqing, an edict excused court audience; after three days it was again transmitted that audience was excused.
translations.idiomatic: On Longqing 1/1/7 an edict canceled court; three days later another notice canceled it again.

sentences.zh: 時亮以新政不宜遽怠，上疏切諫。

translations.literal: Shiliang held that the new reign ought not slacken abruptly; he memorialized with sharp remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang argued the new government should not relax so quickly and submitted a forceful memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋以左給事中副檢討許國使朝鮮。

translations.literal: Soon, as Left Supervising Secretary, he accompanied Reviser Xu Guo on an embassy to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to Korea as Left Supervising Secretary assisting Reviser Xu Guo.

sentences.zh: 故事，王北面聽詔，使者西面。

translations.literal: By precedent the king faced north to hear the edict and the envoy faced west.
translations.idiomatic: Custom held that the king faced north to receive the edict while the envoy faced west.

sentences.zh: 時亮爭之，乃南面宣詔。

translations.literal: Shiliang contested this; the edict was then proclaimed facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang objected, and the edict was read facing south instead.

sentences.zh: 還，進戶科給事中，因列上遼東事宜。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Revenue Section and submitted Liaodong affairs in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he rose to supervising secretary in the Revenue Section and laid out Liaodong policy in full.

sentences.zh: 已，請慎起居，罷遊宴，日禦便殿省章奏，召大臣裁決。

translations.literal: Thereafter he asked that the emperor watch his daily regimen, stop tours and banquets, hold daily informal audience to review memorials, and summon ministers to decide affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged careful daily conduct, an end to pleasure outings, daily review of memorials in the side hall, and summoning ministers for decisions.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: Notice was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 興都莊地八千三百頃，中官奪民田，復增八百頃，立三十六莊。

translations.literal: The Xingdu estates covered eight thousand three hundred qing; eunuchs seized private fields, added eight hundred qing more, and established thirty-six manors.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingdu, on eight thousand three hundred qing of land, eunuchs seized peasant holdings, added eight hundred qing, and set up thirty-six estates.

sentences.zh: 帝從撫按奏，屬有司征租，還兼並者於民。

translations.literal: The emperor followed the provincial governor and censor's memorial, ordered local offices to collect rent, and returned seized land to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the governor-censor report, had local officials collect rents, and restored annexed fields to their owners.

sentences.zh: 中官張堯為請，又許之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhang Yao petitioned on their behalf, and permission was granted again.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Zhang Yao interceded for them, and the emperor again consented.

sentences.zh: 時亮極諫，不納。

translations.literal: Shiliang remonstrated fiercely; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang protested vehemently, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 帝臨朝，拱默未嘗發一言。

translations.literal: When the emperor held court he sat in silence and never uttered a word.
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor remained silent and never spoke.

sentences.zh: 及石州陷，有請帝詰問大臣者。

translations.literal: When Shizhou fell, some asked the emperor to interrogate the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizhou was lost, some urged the emperor to question his ministers.

sentences.zh: 越二日，講罷，帝果問石州破狀。

translations.literal: After two days, when the lecture ended, the emperor indeed asked about the fall of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later, after the lecture, the emperor did ask how Shizhou had fallen.

sentences.zh: 中官王本輒從旁詬諸臣欺蔽。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Ben from the side reviled the ministers for deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Wang Ben interrupted from the side, accusing the ministers of deception.

sentences.zh: 帝慍，目懾之，本猶刺刺語。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and glared to intimidate him, but Ben still kept prattling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flushed with anger and glared at him, yet Ben kept on talking.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and dismissed court.
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor ended the session.

sentences.zh: 時亮劾本無人臣禮，大不敬，且數其不法數事。

translations.literal: Shiliang impeached Ben for lacking a subject's rites, for grave disrespect, and listed several of his illegal acts.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang charged Ben with breach of subject's decorum and lese-majeste, citing several unlawful deeds.

sentences.zh: 疏雖不行，士論壯之。

translations.literal: Although the memorial was not acted upon, public opinion applauded him.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went nowhere, but scholars praised his courage.

sentences.zh: 十月初，詔停日講。

translations.literal: In early tenth month an edict stopped the daily lectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the tenth month the emperor halted daily lectures.

sentences.zh: 時亮率同列言天未冱寒，不宜遽輟。

translations.literal: Shiliang led his colleagues in saying heaven was not yet bitterly cold and the lectures should not be abruptly stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang and his colleagues argued that winter had not yet set in and lectures should not cease so soon.

sentences.zh: 俄請以薛瑄、陳獻章、王守仁從祀文廟，章下所司。

translations.literal: Soon he asked that Xue Xuan, Chen Xianzhang, and Wang Shouren be enshrined in the Confucian temple; the memorial was sent to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: He soon proposed enshrining Xue Xuan, Chen Xianzhang, and Wang Shouren in the Confucian temple; the memorial went to the ministries.

sentences.zh: 又言方春東作，宜敕有司釋輕系，停訟獄，詔可。

translations.literal: He also said that with spring farming beginning, offices should release lightly held prisoners and halt lawsuits; an edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged, as spring planting began, releasing minor detainees and suspending litigation; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年六月言：「今天下大患三：藩祿不給也，邊餉不支也，公私交困也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year he said: "Today's great calamities are three: princely stipends are insufficient, frontier rations cannot be supplied, and public and private interests are both in distress.
translations.idiomatic: The next June he wrote: "The realm faces three grave ills: imperial clans cannot live on their stipends, frontier pay cannot be met, and state and people alike are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 宗藩有一時之計，有百世之計。

translations.literal: The imperial clans have plans for the moment and plans for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: For the clans there are expedients for the present and reforms for the long term.

sentences.zh: 亟立宗學，教之禮讓，祿萬石者歲捐五之一，二千石者十之一，千石者二十之一，以贍貧宗，立為定制。

translations.literal: Urgently establish clan schools and teach courtesy and deference; those with stipends of ten thousand shi should donate one-fifth yearly, those with two thousand one-tenth, those with one thousand one-twentieth, to support poor clansmen, and establish this as a fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Establish clan schools at once to teach ritual and humility; princes receiving ten thousand shi should give one-fifth yearly, two-thousand-shi houses one-tenth, one-thousand-shi houses one-twentieth, to aid poor kinsmen—then fix this as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 此一時計也。

translations.literal: This is the plan for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: That is the short-term remedy.

sentences.zh: 各宗聚居一城，貧日益甚，宜令就近散處，給閑田使耕以代祿；

translations.literal: Clans concentrated in one city grow poorer by the day; they should be scattered nearby and granted idle land to farm in place of stipends;
translations.idiomatic: When clans are packed into one city poverty only deepens; let them settle nearby and work idle fields in lieu of salary;

sentences.zh: 奸生之孽，重行黜削。

translations.literal: Bastards born of illicit unions should be severely demoted and stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Illegitimate offspring should be heavily demoted and cut off.

sentences.zh: 此百世計也。

translations.literal: This is the plan for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: That is the long-term reform.

sentences.zh: 邊餉莫要於屯鹽，近遴大臣龐尚鵬、鄒應龍、淩儒經理，事權雖重，顧往河東者兼理四川，往江北者兼理山東、河南，往江南者兼理浙、湖、雲、貴，重內地而輕塞下，非初旨也。

translations.literal: Frontier rations depend most on garrison salt; recently the ministers Pang Shangpeng, Zou Yinglong, and Ling Ru were chosen to manage it; though their authority was weighty, those sent to Hedong also managed Sichuan, those to Jiangbei also Shandong and Henan, those to Jiangnan also Zhejiang, Huguang, Yunnan, and Guizhou—emphasizing the interior while slighting the frontier camps, contrary to the original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Border pay rests above all on garrison salt; Pang Shangpeng, Zou Yinglong, and Ling Ru were lately put in charge with broad powers, yet the man sent to Hedong also ran Sichuan, the Jiangbei officer also Shandong and Henan, the Jiangnan officer also Zhejiang, Hunan, Yunnan, and Guizhou—weighting the interior and neglecting the frontier, not what was first intended.

sentences.zh: 且一人領數道，曠遠難周。

translations.literal: Moreover one man overseeing several circuits—too vast to cover thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: And one man cannot oversee several distant circuits at once.

sentences.zh: 請在內地者專責巡撫，令尚鵬等三人分任塞下屯事，久任責成，有功待以不次，則利興而邊儲自裕。

translations.literal: He asked that officials in the interior be charged solely to provincial governors, and that Shangpeng and the other three divide frontier garrison salt affairs; with long tenure and accountability, merit rewarded with extraordinary promotion—then profits would rise and frontier stores would naturally suffice.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed leaving interior salt to the governors while Shangpeng and the others each took a frontier zone, with long terms, clear responsibility, and exceptional rewards for success—then revenue would grow and border granaries fill themselves.

sentences.zh: 今天下府庫殫虛，百姓困瘁，而建議者欲罄天下庫藏輸內府，以濟旦夕之用。

translations.literal: Today the empire's treasuries are exhausted and the people are worn down, yet advisers wish to drain all stores under heaven into the inner court to meet immediate needs.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial coffers are empty and the people are exhausted, yet some counsel emptying every treasury into the inner palace for day-to-day spending.

sentences.zh: 脫州郡有變，何以待之？

translations.literal: If provinces and commanderies rise in revolt, how then shall we respond?
translations.idiomatic: If the regions revolt, what reserves will we have?

sentences.zh: 夫守令以養民為職，要在勸農桑、清徭賦、重鄉約、嚴保甲，而簿書獄訟、催科巧拙不與焉。」

translations.literal: Magistrates and prefects take nurturing the people as their duty; the essentials are encouraging farming and sericulture, clearing corvée levies, honoring village compacts, and tightening baojia organization—while skill in ledgers, litigation, and tax collection does not enter into it."
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates exist to sustain the people: promote farming, lighten levies, enforce village compacts, tighten baojia—paperwork, lawsuits, and tax tricks are not the measure."

sentences.zh: 疏上，多議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, much of it was discussed for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the memorial was debated and largely adopted.

sentences.zh: 其冬，復疏言：「天下可憂在民窮，能為民紓憂者，知府而已，宜慎重其選。

translations.literal: That winter he again memorialized: "What is worrisome under heaven is the people's poverty; only prefects can ease that worry—their selection should be made with care.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he wrote again: "The nation's worry is popular poverty, and only prefects can relieve it—choose them with utmost care.

sentences.zh: 治行卓越，即擢京卿若巡撫，則人自激勸。

translations.literal: Where governance is outstanding, immediately promote to capital minister or provincial governor—then others will be inspired of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Promote outstanding prefects straight to capital office or a governorship, and others will strive on their own.

sentences.zh: 督學者，天下名教所系，當擇學行兼懋者，毋限以時。

translations.literal: Education commissioners bind the empire's name and teaching; choose those excelling in both learning and conduct, without limiting by schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial education commissioners uphold the realm's culture—pick men of proven scholarship and character, not by rotation alone.

sentences.zh: 教行望峻，則召為祭酒或入翰林，以示風勵。」

translations.literal: Where teaching is distinguished and reputation lofty, summon as Chancellor of the National University or admit to the Hanlin, to show encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: When their teaching is eminent, call them to be Grand Master of the National University or into the Hanlin as a mark of honor."

sentences.zh: 下部議，卒不行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries for discussion; in the end it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated, but in the end nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢太仆少卿。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was made vice director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 初，徐階、高拱相構，時亮與朝臣攻去拱。

translations.literal: Initially Xu Jie and Gao Gong opposed each other; Shiliang joined court ministers in attacking to drive Gong away.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xu Jie and Gao Gong were at odds; Shiliang and others in court helped force Gong out.

sentences.zh: 已而拱復入，考察言官，排異己者；

translations.literal: Later Gong returned, evaluated censorial officials, and expelled those who differed from him;
translations.idiomatic: When Gong came back he reviewed the censorate and purged dissenters;

sentences.zh: 時亮及陳瓚、張槚已擢京卿，皆被斥。

translations.literal: Shiliang, Chen Zan, and Zhang Hao had already been promoted to capital ministers—all were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang, Chen Zan, and Zhang Hao, though already raised to capital posts, were all driven out.

sentences.zh: 時亮坐不謹，落職。

translations.literal: Shiliang was punished for imprudence and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang was faulted for lack of discretion and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十二年，用丘橓、余懋學等薦，起南京大理丞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Wanli, on the recommendation of Qiu Yin, Yu Maoxue, and others, he was recalled as assistant director of the Nanjing Court of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 12 brought his recall to Nanjing assistant director of Punishments, on the recommendation of Qiu Yin and Yu Maoxue.

sentences.zh: 累遷右副都御史，攝京營戎政，陳安攘要務十四事。

translations.literal: He rose through accumulated promotions to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, acted in Beijing garrison military affairs, and submitted fourteen key points on pacification.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, took charge of capital garrison affairs, and laid out fourteen essentials of defense and order.

sentences.zh: 尋請以水利、義倉、生養、賦役、清獄、弭盜、善俗七條課守令，歲終報部院及科，計吏時以修廢定殿最。

translations.literal: Soon he asked that magistrates be graded on seven items—hydraulics, charity granaries, livelihood, taxes and corvée, clearing prisons, quelling bandits, and improving customs—with year-end reports to ministries, provincial offices, and the censorate, and evaluation officers ranking them by achievement and failure.
translations.idiomatic: He next proposed grading prefects and magistrates on seven counts—waterworks, relief granaries, livelihood, taxation, clearing jails, suppressing bandits, and improving custom—with annual reports to ministries and censors to set their rankings.

sentences.zh: 又請皇長子出閣講學。

translations.literal: He also asked that the heir apparent leave the inner quarters for lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the crown prince to leave the palace for formal study.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部左、右侍郎，拜南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Justice and was appointed Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through both vice ministries of Justice and became Nanjing minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒官。

translations.literal: After a year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died in post.

sentences.zh: 時亮初好交遊，負意氣。

translations.literal: Shiliang early on loved socializing and was proud in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Shiliang was sociable and high-spirited.

sentences.zh: 嘗劾罷左都御史張永明，為時論所非。

translations.literal: He once impeached Left Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yongming from office and was criticized by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: He once forced Left Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yongming from office, to the disapproval of his peers.

sentences.zh: 時亮亦悔之。

translations.literal: Shiliang also came to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Later he regretted that act.

sentences.zh: 中遭挫抑，潛心性理之學。

translations.literal: After mid-career setbacks he cultivated the learning of principle inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Setbacks in mid-career turned him inward to moral philosophy.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，謚莊靖。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was given the posthumous name Zhuangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he received the posthumous name Zhuangjing ("Solemn and Tranquil").

sentences.zh: 陳瓚，字廷稞，常熟人。

translations.literal: Chen Zan, styled Tingke, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zan, courtesy name Tingke, came from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing he passed the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Jiajing 35.

sentences.zh: 授江西永豐知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Yongfeng, Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 治最，擢刑科給事中。

translations.literal: His administration was rated highest, and he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Justice section.
translations.idiomatic: Rated top in administrative merit, he was raised to supervising secretary in the Justice section.

sentences.zh: 劾罷嚴嵩黨祭酒王才、諭德唐汝楫。

translations.literal: He impeached and had removed Yan Song's partisans, Grand Master of Sacrifices Wang Cai and Preceptor Tang Rujie.
translations.idiomatic: He brought down Yan Song allies Grand Master of Sacrifices Wang Cai and Preceptor Tang Rujie through impeachment.

sentences.zh: 遷左給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved up to Left Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 劾文選郎南軒，請錄建言廢斥者。

translations.literal: He impeached Selection Bureau director Nan Xuan and requested that memorialists who had been dismissed for remonstrance be restored.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Selection Bureau director Nan Xuan and asked that officials expelled for speaking out be reinstated.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，杖六十除名。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, had him beaten sixty strokes, and struck his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, had him thrashed sixty blows, and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，起官吏科，請恤楊最、楊爵、羅洪先、楊繼盛，而誅奸黨之殺沈煉者。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he was recalled to the Ministry of Personnel section and requested posthumous honors for Yang Zui, Yang Jue, Luo Hongxian, and Yang Jisheng, and execution of the villainous faction that had killed Shen Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled in Longqing 1 to the Personnel section, he sought honors for Yang Zui, Yang Jue, Luo Hongxian, and Yang Jisheng and punishment for the clique that murdered Shen Lian.

sentences.zh: 帝可之，楊順、路楷皆逮治。

translations.literal: The emperor approved; Yang Shun and Lu Kai were both arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented, and Yang Shun and Lu Kai were both seized for trial.

sentences.zh: 其冬，擢太常少卿。

translations.literal: That winter he was promoted to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was made Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 高拱惡瓚為徐階所引，瓚已移疾歸，竟坐浮躁謫洛川丞，不赴。

translations.literal: Gao Gong hated Zan as a man introduced by Xu Jie; Zan had already resigned citing illness, but in the end was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Luochuan for frivolity and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong resented Zan as Xu Jie's protégé; though Zan had already gone home on sick leave, he was finally banished to Luochuan assistant magistrate for rashness and never reported.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，累官刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign he rose through successive posts to Left Vice Minister of Justice.
