translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli era he eventually reached Left Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 初，瓚為拱所惡，被斥，及張居正柄政，亦惡之，不召。

translations.literal: At first Zan had been hated by Gao Gong and expelled; when Zhang Juzheng held power he also disliked him and would not recall him.
translations.idiomatic: Zan had first been driven out by Gao Gong; under Zhang Juzheng's dominance he was likewise disliked and left unreappointed.

sentences.zh: 居正死，始以薦起會稽縣丞。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died he was at last raised on recommendation to Assistant Magistrate of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Juzheng's death was he recommended back as Assistant Magistrate of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 其後官侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he reached the rank of vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to vice minister.

sentences.zh: 稽勛郎顧憲成疏論時弊謫官，瓚責大學士王錫爵曰：「憲成疏最公，何以得譴？」

translations.literal: When Record Office director Gu Xiancheng memorialized on current abuses and was demoted, Zan rebuked Grand Secretary Wang Xijue, saying, "Xiancheng's memorial was utterly fair—why was he punished?"
translations.idiomatic: After Record Office director Gu Xiancheng was banished for criticizing abuses of the day, Zan confronted Grand Secretary Wang Xijue: "Xiancheng's memorial was entirely just—why was he punished?"

sentences.zh: 錫爵曰：「彼執書生之言，徇道旁之口，安知吾輩苦心。」

translations.literal: Xijue said, "He clings to a bookish view and follows roadside gossip—how could he know the pains we take."
translations.idiomatic: Xijue replied, "He clings to pedantic talk and heeds street rumor—how could he grasp our difficulties."

sentences.zh: 瓚曰：「恐書生之言當信，道旁之口當察，憲成苦心亦不可不知也。」

translations.literal: Zan said, "I fear the bookish view should be trusted, roadside gossip should be examined, and Xiancheng's pains also should not go unknown."
translations.idiomatic: Zan answered, "Perhaps pedantic counsel deserves trust, street talk deserves scrutiny, and Xiancheng's concerns deserve heed as well."

sentences.zh: 錫爵默然。

translations.literal: Xijue fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue said nothing.

sentences.zh: 瓚前後忤執政如此。

translations.literal: Thus did Zan repeatedly defy those in power.
translations.idiomatic: In this way Zan repeatedly crossed the men at the helm.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈右都御史，謚莊靖。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief, with the posthumous title Zhuangjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Censor-in-Chief with the posthumous name Zhuangjing.

sentences.zh: 槚見《鄒應龍傳》。

translations.literal: Qiao is treated in the Zou Yinglong biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang is treated in the Zou Yinglong biography.

sentences.zh: 郝傑，字彥輔，蔚州人。

translations.literal: Hao Jie, courtesy name Yanfu, was a native of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Jie, styled Yanfu, came from Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父銘，御史。

translations.literal: His father Ming was a censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ming had served as censor.

sentences.zh: 傑舉嘉靖三十五年進士，授行人，擢御史。

translations.literal: Jie passed the palace examination in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing, was appointed courier, and was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jie became a jinshi in Jiajing 35, served as courier, and was raised to censor.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，巡撫畿輔。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he served as grand coordinator of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 he was grand coordinator of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 冬，寇大入永平，疏請蠲被掠地徭賦，且言：「比年罰行於文臣而於武弁，及於主帥而略於偏裨，請飭法以振國威。」

translations.literal: In winter, when bandits made a major incursion into Yongping, he memorialized requesting remission of corvée and taxes for ravaged districts, and said, "In recent years punishments have fallen on civil officials but spared military officers, and on commanders while overlooking subordinate officers—please tighten the law to restore national prestige."
translations.idiomatic: That winter, after raiders struck Yongping in force, he asked that levies be waived in plundered areas and wrote, "Punishment lately hits civil officials but not military men, and commanders but not their juniors—discipline the code to restore imperial authority."

sentences.zh: 俱報可。

translations.literal: Both requests were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 已，劾薊督劉燾、巡撫耿隨卿觀望，寇退則斷死者報首功，又奪遼東將士棒槌崖戰績，並論副使沈應乾，遊擊李信、周冕罪。

translations.literal: Later he impeached Jizhou Superintendent Liu Tao and Grand Coordinator Geng Suiqing for standing idle; when the bandits withdrew they reported severed heads of the dead as merit, and he also stripped the Liaodong officers of their Bangchuiya victory credit, jointly charging Vice Commissioner Shen Yingqian and battalion commanders Li Xin and Zhou Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He then charged Jizhou Superintendent Liu Tao and Grand Coordinator Geng Suiqing with holding back; after the raiders withdrew they claimed credit with severed heads of the slain, and he also stripped Liaodong troops of Bangchuiya battle honors while indicting Vice Commissioner Shen Yingqian and battalion commanders Li Xin and Zhou Mian.

sentences.zh: 帝為黜應乾，下信、冕獄，敕燾、隨卿還籍聽勘。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Shen Yingqian, imprisoned Li Xin and Zhou Mian, and ordered Tao and Suiqing to return to their native places pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne removed Shen Yingqian, jailed Li Xin and Zhou Mian, and sent Tao and Suiqing home to await inquiry.

sentences.zh: 詔遣中官李祐督蘇、杭織造，工部執奏，不從。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched eunuch Li You to supervise weaving in Suzhou and Hangzhou; the Ministry of Works submitted a firm memorial in opposition, but the emperor would not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered eunuch Li You to oversee Suzhou and Hangzhou weaving; the Ministry of Works protested in memorial, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 傑言：「登極詔書罷織造甫一年，敕使復遣，非畫一之政。

translations.literal: Jie said, "The accession edict abolished weaving only a year ago, yet an imperial envoy has been sent again—this is not uniform policy.
translations.idiomatic: Jie argued, "The enthronement edict ended weaving only a year ago, yet an envoy has been dispatched again—policy is no longer consistent.

sentences.zh: 且內臣專恣，有司剝下奉之，損聖德非小。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when eunuchs act arbitrarily, local officials squeeze the people to supply them—this is no small injury to imperial virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Worse, eunuchs rule unchecked while officials squeeze the populace to feed them—a serious blow to the throne's reputation."

sentences.zh: 帝終不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor still would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still ignored him.

sentences.zh: 駕幸南海子，命京營諸軍盡從。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Southern Park, he ordered all capital garrison troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: On an imperial visit to the Southern Park, all capital garrison troops were ordered to accompany the procession.

sentences.zh: 徐階、楊博等諫，不聽，傑復爭之，卒不從。

translations.literal: Xu Jie, Yang Bo, and others remonstrated but were not heeded; Jie protested again, and in the end the emperor still would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie, Yang Bo, and others remonstrated in vain; Jie protested again, and the emperor still refused.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎洪朝選以拾遺罷，上疏自辨，傑等劾其違制，遂削職。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Hong Chaoxuan was dismissed for a supplemental impeachment; he submitted a memorial in self-defense, and Jie and others impeached him for violating regulations, whereupon his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Hong Chaoxuan was removed after a supplemental impeachment; when he memorialized in self-defense, Jie and others charged him with breaking protocol and he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 以嘗論高拱非宰輔器，為所嫉。

translations.literal: Because he had once argued that Gao Gong was unfit to be chief minister, he was hated by Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He had once declared Gao Gong unfit for the premiership, and Gao resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 及拱再召，傑遂請急去。

translations.literal: When Gao was recalled again, Jie promptly requested urgent leave to depart.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao returned to power, Jie immediately sought leave to quit.

sentences.zh: 拱罷，起故官。

translations.literal: After Gao was dismissed, Jie was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao fell, Jie was reinstated in his old office.

sentences.zh: 旋以私議張居正逐拱非是，出為陜西副使。

translations.literal: Soon, because he had privately said that Zhang Juzheng's expulsion of Gao Gong was wrong, he was sent out as Shaanxi Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted to Shaanxi as vice commissioner after privately criticizing Zhang Juzheng's ouster of Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 再遷山東左布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was next promoted to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 被劾，降遼東苑馬寺卿兼海道兵備，加山東按察使。

translations.literal: Impeached, he was demoted to Director of the Liaodong Stud Farm and concurrent coastal defense commissioner, with the added rank of Shandong Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After impeachment he was reduced to Liaodong Stud Farm director with concurrent coastal defense duties, and given the additional title Shandong Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢右僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen he became Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 以督諸將擊敵，錄一子官。

translations.literal: For directing the generals in striking the enemy, one of his sons was granted an official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Because he directed the generals against the enemy, one son received an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 時李成梁為總兵官，威望甚著，然上功不無抵欺。

translations.literal: At the time Li Chengliang was regional commander, and though his prestige was great, his merit reports were not without fabrication.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengliang was then regional commander: widely feared, yet not above falsifying battle credit.

sentences.zh: 寇入塞，或斂兵避，既退，始尾襲老弱，或乘虛搗零部，誘殺附塞者充首功，習以為常。

translations.literal: When bandits entered the frontier, he would sometimes hold his troops back; only after they withdrew would he trail and strike the old and weak, or raid scattered bands when they were exposed, or lure and kill frontier dependents to pass off as head-count merit—a practice become routine.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders crossed the border he sometimes held back; after they withdrew he would pick off the aged and weak, raid isolated bands, or slaughter frontier dependents for false head counts—a settled habit.

sentences.zh: 督撫諸臣庇之，傑獨不與比。

translations.literal: Supervising officials shielded him, but Jie alone would not go along.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising and coordinating officials covered for him; Jie alone refused to join them.

sentences.zh: 十九年春，成梁用參將郭夢徵策，使副將李寧襲板升於鎮夷堡，獲老弱二百八十余級。

translations.literal: In the spring of the nineteenth year, Chengliang, using Battalion Commander Guo Mengzheng's plan, sent Vice Commander Li Ning to raid Ban Sheng at Zhenyi Fort and took more than two hundred eighty heads of the old and weak.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year nineteen Chengliang, following Battalion Commander Guo Mengzheng's scheme, sent Vice Commander Li Ning to strike Ban Sheng at Zhenyi Fort and claimed over two hundred eighty heads of old and weak captives.

sentences.zh: 師旋，為別部所遮，寧先走，將士數千人失亡大半，成梁飾功邀敘。

translations.literal: As the army returned it was intercepted by another band; Ning fled first, and several thousand officers and soldiers were lost—more than half the force—yet Chengliang embellished the achievement to seek reward.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home another band blocked them; Ning ran first and several thousand troops were lost—well over half—yet Chengliang dressed up the affair to claim honors.

sentences.zh: 傑具奏草，直言其故，要總督蹇達共奏。

translations.literal: Jie prepared a full draft memorial stating the facts plainly and insisted that Governor-General Jian Da submit jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Jie drafted a full memorial stating the facts and demanded that Governor-General Jian Da co-submit it.

sentences.zh: 達匿其草，自為奏論功。

translations.literal: Da concealed Jie's draft and submitted his own memorial discussing merit.
translations.idiomatic: Da hid Jie's draft and filed his own memorial praising the victory.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史胡克儉馳疏劾寧，詞連成梁，亦詆傑。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Hu Kejian rushed a memorial impeaching Ning, implicating Chengliang in the wording and also denigrating Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Hu Kejian hurried a memorial against Ning, linking Chengliang in the charges and attacking Jie as well.

sentences.zh: 兵部置寧罪不議。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War set Ning's offense aside without deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War declined to consider Ning's crimes.

sentences.zh: 克儉大憤，盡發成梁、達隱蔽狀。

translations.literal: Kejian was greatly indignant and fully exposed Chengliang's and Da's concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian, furious, laid bare all Chengliang's and Da's cover-ups.

sentences.zh: 先是，十八年冬，海州被掠十三日，副將孫守廉不戰，成梁亦弗救。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the winter of the eighteenth year, Haizhou had been plundered for thirteen days; Vice Commander Sun Shoulian did not fight, and Chengliang also did not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, in winter of year eighteen Haizhou had been ravaged for thirteen days; Vice Commander Sun Shoulian never fought, and Chengliang never relieved the town.

sentences.zh: 克儉既劾守謙，申時行、許國庇之，止令聽勘。

translations.literal: After Kejian had impeached Shoulian, Shen Shihang and Xu Guo shielded him, and the court only ordered him to await investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian had impeached Shoulian, but Shen Shihang and Xu Guo protected him, and the court merely ordered him to await inquiry.

sentences.zh: 克儉乃言：「臣初劾守廉，時行以書沮臣；

translations.literal: Kejian then said, "When I first impeached Shoulian, Shihang wrote to obstruct me;
translations.idiomatic: Kejian then wrote, "When I first impeached Shoulian, Shihang tried to block me by letter;

sentences.zh: 及劾寧，又與國諭臣寬其罪。

translations.literal: when I impeached Ning, he again joined Xu Guo in instructing me to leniently treat his crime.
translations.idiomatic: when I impeached Ning, he and Xu Guo urged me to soften the charges.

sentences.zh: 徇私背公，將壞邊事。」

translations.literal: Favoring private ties and betraying public duty will ruin frontier affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Private favor over public duty will wreck frontier defense."

sentences.zh: 並歷詆一鶚、達及兵科給事中張應登朋奸欺罔，達置傑會稿功罪疏不奏，遂追數成梁前數年冒功狀。

translations.literal: He also successively denounced Shen Yiyu, Da, and Ministry of War supervising secretary Zhang Yingdeng as a clique of villains practicing deceit; Da had shelved Jie's joint draft on merit and guilt and would not submit it, and he then traced Chengliang's false merit claims of prior years.
translations.idiomatic: He also denounced Shen Yiyu, Da, and Ministry of War supervising secretary Zhang Yingdeng as a deceitful clique; Da had suppressed Jie's joint memorial on merit and guilt, and he now traced years of Chengliang's inflated victories.

sentences.zh: 帝謂成梁前功皆由巡按勘報，克儉懸度妄議。

translations.literal: The emperor said Chengliang's earlier achievements had all been verified by investigating censors, and that Kejian's suspicions were reckless speculation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that Chengliang's earlier feats had been confirmed by investigating censors and that Kejian's charges were groundless surmise.

sentences.zh: 卒置成梁等不問，而心以傑為不欺。

translations.literal: In the end Chengliang and the others went unpunished, but in his heart the emperor regarded Jie as honest.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang and the rest were left untouched, yet the emperor inwardly judged Jie trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 旋就進右副都御史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 日本陷朝鮮，達遣裨將祖承訓以三千人往，皆沒。

translations.literal: When Japan overran Korea, Da sent Lieutenant Commander Zu Chengxun with three thousand men, and all were lost.
translations.idiomatic: After Japan overran Korea, Da sent Lieutenant Commander Zu Chengxun with three thousand troops; all perished.

sentences.zh: 事聞，傑亦被劾，帝特免之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Jie was also impeached, but the emperor specially exempted him.
translations.idiomatic: When news arrived Jie was impeached too, but the emperor expressly spared him.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮王避難將入遼，傑請擇境外善地處之，且周給其從官、衛士，報可。

translations.literal: As the king of Korea sought refuge and was about to enter Liaodong, Jie requested that a suitable place outside the border be chosen to receive him and that his attendants and guards be fully supplied; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: With the Korean king fleeing toward Liaodong, Jie asked that he be lodged at a safe site beyond the border and that his retinue be provided for; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋遷兵部右侍郎，總督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of War and made governor-general of Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Right Vice Minister of War and governor-general of Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 召理戎政，進右都御史。

translations.literal: Recalled to manage military administration, he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to direct military affairs, he rose to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 日本封貢議起，傑曰：「平秀吉罪不勝誅，顧加以爵命，荒外聞之，謂中朝無人。」

translations.literal: When debate arose over Japan's investiture and tribute mission, Jie said, "Hideyoshi's crimes deserve death beyond measure, yet to grant him rank and title—when the wild borderlands hear of it, they will say the Middle Kingdom has no men."
translations.idiomatic: When Japan's enfeoffment and tribute were debated, Jie declared, "Hideyoshi's crimes cry out for execution, yet if we grant him rank and titles, the outer world will say the court has no worthy men."

sentences.zh: 議不合，徙南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: His view did not prevail, and he was transferred to Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Overruled, he was moved to Nanjing Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸。

translations.literal: He resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home on sick leave.

sentences.zh: 起南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Minister of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Nanjing Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 就改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: He was immediately changed to the Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once shifted to the Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 胡克儉，字共之，光山人。

translations.literal: Hu Kejian, courtesy name Gongzhi, was a native of Guangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Kejian, styled Gongzhi, came from Guangshan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the palace examination in the fourteenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Wanli 14.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士改御史，巡按山東。

translations.literal: From Hanlin Bachelor he was transferred to censor and sent to investigate Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the Hanlin Academy, he became investigating censor for Shandong.

sentences.zh: 遼東其所轄也，奏禁買功、竊級諸弊。

translations.literal: Liaodong was within his jurisdiction, and he memorialized forbidding the abuses of buying merit and stealing credit.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong fell under his circuit, and he memorialized to ban purchased merit and stolen battle credit.

sentences.zh: 既劾成梁，為要人所忌。

translations.literal: After he impeached Chengliang he was hated by powerful men.
translations.idiomatic: Once he impeached Chengliang, men of influence turned against him.

sentences.zh: 會克儉劾左都御史李世達曲庇罪囚，至詆為賊，執政遂言克儉妄排執法大臣，不可居言路，謫蘄水丞。

translations.literal: When Kejian impeached Left Censor-in-Chief Li Shida for bending the law to shield criminals, even denouncing him as a bandit, the ruling faction said Kejian was recklessly attacking law-enforcing grandees and was unfit for the remonstrance posts, and he was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Qishui.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian charged Left Censor-in-Chief Li Shida with shielding criminals, even calling him a traitor; the ruling faction declared him unfit for the censorate and banished him to Qishui assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 上官以事遣歸，裏居三十年。

translations.literal: His superiors sent him home on account of the affair, and he lived in retirement for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Sent home over the affair, he remained in private life for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，起光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong acceded, he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangzong's accession he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，歷刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he served successively as Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi era he rose to Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，逆黨李恒茂論其衰朽，落職歸。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year the factionalist Li Hengmao attacked him as senile, and he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of year five the factionalist Li Hengmao denounced him as decrepit and he was removed.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 卒贈尚書。

translations.literal: Upon death he was posthumously made Minister.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was posthumously made Minister.

sentences.zh: 克儉本姓扶，冒胡姓，久之始復故。

translations.literal: Kejian's original surname was Fu; he had usurped the Hu surname and only after a long time restored the old one.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian was born Fu but had taken the surname Hu, restoring his original name only after many years.

sentences.zh: 趙參魯

translations.literal: Zhao Canlu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Canlu

sentences.zh: 趙參魯，字宗傳，鄞人。

translations.literal: Zhao Canlu, courtesy name Zongchuan, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Canlu, styled Zongchuan, came from Yin.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the palace examination in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Longqing 5.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，改戶科給事中。

translations.literal: Selected as Hanlin Bachelor, he was transferred to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen as Hanlin Bachelor, he moved to supervising secretary in the Revenue section.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年，慈聖太后立廟涿州，祀碧霞元君。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli the Empress Dowager Cisheng erected a temple at Zhuozhou to worship the Goddess Bixia.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 2 Empress Dowager Cisheng built a temple at Zhuozhou to the Goddess Bixia.

sentences.zh: 部科臣執奏，不從。

translations.literal: Ministry and censorate officials submitted firm memorials in opposition, but the emperor would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry and censorate officials protested in memorial, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 參魯斥其不經，且言：「南北被寇，流害生民，興役浚河，鬻及妻子。

translations.literal: Canlu denounced the project as irregular and said, "North and south have suffered bandit raids, bringing harm to the people; labor for river dredging has forced them even to sell wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Canlu condemned the rite as improper and wrote, "Bandits have ravaged north and south, ruining the people; dredging levies have driven families to sell even wives and children.

sentences.zh: 陛下發帑治橋建廟，已五萬有奇。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already spent more than fifty thousand taels from the treasury to repair bridges and build temples.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already drawn over fifty thousand taels from the treasury for bridges and temples.

sentences.zh: 茍移振貧民，植福當更大。」

translations.literal: If this were shifted to relief for the poor, the merit accrued would be greater."
translations.idiomatic: Redirected to famine relief, the blessing would be far greater."

sentences.zh: 亦不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor still would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still ignored the plea.

sentences.zh: 南京中官張進醉辱給事中王頤，給事中鄭嶽、楊節交章論，未報，參魯復上言：「進乃守備中官申信黨，不並治信，無以厭人心。」

translations.literal: At Nanjing the eunuch Zhang Jin, drunk, insulted supervising secretary Wang Yi; supervising secretaries Zheng Yue and Yang Jie submitted successive memorials on the matter, but no reply came, and Canlu memorialized again, saying, "Jin is a follower of the garrison eunuch Shen Xin—unless Xin is punished along with him, popular sentiment cannot be satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing eunuch Zhang Jin drunkenly humiliated supervising secretary Wang Yi, Zheng Yue and Yang Jie memorialized in protest without response; Canlu added, "Jin belongs to garrison eunuch Shen Xin's faction—unless Xin is punished too, the public will not be appeased.

sentences.zh: 時信方結馮保，朝議遂奪嶽等俸，謫參魯高安典史。

translations.literal: At that time Xin was then allied with Feng Bao; court deliberation thereupon stripped Yue and the others of salary and demoted Canlu to Gao'an county archivist.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xin was then in league with Feng Bao, and court opinion turned against the memorialists: Yue and the others lost their stipends, and Canlu was banished to the post of county recorder at Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 遷饒州推官，擢福建提學僉事，請急歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate's assistant at Raozhou, promoted to Fujian educational commissioner, and requested urgent leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Later transferred to magistrate's assistant at Raozhou and promoted to educational commissioner in Fujian, he soon petitioned to hurry home on urgent leave.

sentences.zh: 遭喪，服除，仍督學福建。

translations.literal: He suffered bereavement; after mourning ended, he still supervised education in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: After a death in the family and completion of mourning, he returned to his educational duties in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 歷南京太常卿。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of Ceremonies at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through service to Vice Minister of Ceremonies in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以右副都御史巡撫福建。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he became Grand Coordinator of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 17 he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Fujian with the rank of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 申嚴海禁，戮奸商通倭者。

translations.literal: He strictly enforced the maritime ban and executed treacherous merchants who trafficked with the Japanese.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened the coastal prohibition and put to death merchants who colluded with Japanese pirates.

sentences.zh: 遷大理卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部左侍郎，改兵部，旋改吏部。

translations.literal: Summoned as Left Vice Minister of Punishments, transferred to War, then soon transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Left Vice Minister of Justice, reassigned to War and then shortly to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 日本封貢議起，參魯持不可。

translations.literal: When debate arose over granting Japanese titles and tribute, Canlu maintained it was unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: As the proposal to enfeoff Japan and receive its tribute came up, Canlu held firm that it must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 總督顧養謙不懌，爭於朝，且言參魯熟倭情，宜任。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Gu Yangqian was displeased, argued in court, and said Canlu knew Japanese affairs well and ought to be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Gu Yangqian took offense, disputed the point at court, and argued that Canlu understood Japanese affairs and should be given the task.

sentences.zh: 章下廷臣，參魯復持前說，因著《東封三議》，辨利害甚悉。

translations.literal: The memorial went to court officials; Canlu again held to his earlier view, and wrote Three Discourses on Eastern Enfeoffment, clarifying benefits and harms in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the court for discussion, Canlu restated his position and composed Three Discourses on Eastern Enfeoffment, setting out the pros and cons with thorough clarity.

sentences.zh: 其後封事卒不成。

translations.literal: Afterward the enfeoffment proposal ultimately failed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the enfeoffment scheme came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 拜南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Justice at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 誠意伯劉世延妄指星象，欲起兵勤王，被劾下吏，參魯當以死。

translations.literal: Marquis of Chengyi Liu Shiyan falsely cited omens in the stars, wishing to raise troops to aid the throne; impeached and handed to the magistrates, Canlu sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Chengyi, Liu Shiyan, had falsely read the stars and plotted to raise troops in the name of saving the throne; once impeached and brought before the courts, Canlu ruled that he deserved death.

sentences.zh: 南京工部主事趙學仕以侵牟為侍郎周思敬所劾，擬戍。

translations.literal: Nanjing Ministry of Works director Zhao Xueshi was impeached by Vice Minister Zhou Sijing for extortion; exile was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xueshi, a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works, was impeached by Vice Minister Zhou Sijing for profiteering, and exile was recommended.

sentences.zh: 學仕移罪家僮，法司予輕比。

translations.literal: Xueshi shifted blame to his household servants; the judicial office gave a lenient sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Xueshi transferred guilt to his household servants, and the judicial authorities imposed a light penalty.

sentences.zh: 御史朱吾弼復劾之，並及參魯，言學仕乃大學士誌臯族父，故參魯庇之。

translations.literal: Censor Zhu Wubi impeached again, also implicating Canlu, saying Xueshi was a kinsman of Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao, hence Canlu shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhu Wubi renewed the impeachment and extended it to Canlu, charging that Xueshi was a kinsman of Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao and that Canlu had protected him for that reason.

sentences.zh: 參魯乞休。

translations.literal: Canlu requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Canlu asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書孫丕揚等言參魯履行素高，不當聽其去，詔留之。

translations.literal: Personnel Minister Sun Piyang and others said Canlu's conduct had always been honorable and he should not be allowed to leave; an edict kept him.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel Minister Sun Piyang and others argued that Canlu's record had always been upright and that he ought not be permitted to resign; the throne ordered him to remain.

sentences.zh: 累加太子太保。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually raised to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 致仕，卒，謚端簡。

translations.literal: He retired, died, and was given the posthumous title Duansu.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office, died, and was posthumously honored with the title Duansu.

sentences.zh: 張孟男

translations.literal: Zhang Mengnan
translations.idiomatic: The biography turns to Zhang Mengnan.

sentences.zh: 張孟男，字元嗣，中牟人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mengnan, courtesy name Yuansi, was a native of Zhongmu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mengnan, styled Yuansi, came from Zhongmu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Jiajing he passed the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Jiajing 44.

sentences.zh: 授廣平推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate's assistant at Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate's assistant at Guangping.

sentences.zh: 稍遷漢中同知。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to subprefect of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later moved up to subprefect of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 入為順天治中，累進尚寶丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as judicial assistant of Shuntian and was cumulatively promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Seals.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital as judicial assistant of Shuntian, he rose step by step to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Seals.

sentences.zh: 高拱以內閣兼吏部，其妻，孟男姑也，自公事外無私語。

translations.literal: Gao Gong held the Grand Secretariat concurrently with Personnel; his wife was Mengnan's aunt by marriage; apart from public business they had no private conversation.
translations.idiomatic: While Gao Gong served in the Grand Secretariat and also headed Personnel, his wife was Mengnan's aunt by marriage, yet beyond official matters they exchanged no private words.

sentences.zh: 拱憾之，四歲不遷。

translations.literal: Gong resented this; for four years no promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Gong took offense at this, and for four years Mengnan received no advancement.

sentences.zh: 及拱被逐，親知皆引匿，孟男獨留拱邸，為治裝送之郊。

translations.literal: When Gong was expelled, friends and kin all hid themselves; Mengnan alone remained at Gong's residence, prepared his baggage and saw him off to the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: After Gong was driven from office, friends and relatives all kept their distance, but Mengnan alone stayed at Gong's house, helped him pack, and escorted him to the city outskirts.

sentences.zh: 張居正用事，擢孟男太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng held power and promoted Mengnan to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Juzheng came to power, he raised Mengnan to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 孟男復不附，失居正意，不調。

translations.literal: Mengnan again would not attach himself; he lost Juzheng's favor and received no transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Mengnan again refused to court favor, fell from Juzheng's good graces, and was passed over for further appointments.

sentences.zh: 久之，居正敗，始累遷南京工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: After long delay, when Juzheng fell, he was cumulatively promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Juzheng's downfall, and after a long wait, was he gradually promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 尋召入，以本官掌通政司事。

translations.literal: Soon summoned to the capital, holding his rank he managed affairs of the Office for Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the capital and, retaining his rank, took charge of the Office for Transmission.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十七年，帝不視朝者八月，孟男疏諫，且言：「嶺南人訟故都御史李材功，蔡人訟故令曹世卿枉，章並留中，其人系兵馬司，橐饘不繼，莫必其生，虧損聖德。」

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli the emperor had not held court for eight months; Mengnan remonstrated and also said: people of Lingnan petitioned on behalf of the late Censor-in-Chief Li Cai's merits, and people of Cai petitioned on behalf of the late Magistrate Cao Shiqing's wrongful treatment; the memorials all remained withheld, the men held at the Horse and Chariot Office with no steady food, their lives uncertain — this damages the emperor's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 17, after eight months without holding court, Mengnan submitted a remonstrance noting that southerners were pleading the case of the late Censor-in-Chief Li Cai while the people of Cai were protesting the injustice done to the late Magistrate Cao Shiqing; with those petitions still held back and the petitioners detained at the Horse and Chariot Office, barely fed and facing uncertain survival, the throne's moral standing was being harmed.

sentences.zh: 帝心動，乃間一禦門。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart was moved and he occasionally held court at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by this, the emperor began to hold court at the gate from time to time.

sentences.zh: 其冬，改戶部，進左侍郎。

translations.literal: That winter he was transferred to Revenue and promoted Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he moved to Revenue and was advanced to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 尋拜南京工部尚書，就改戶部。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Nanjing Minister of Works, then immediately changed to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Nanjing Minister of Works and then immediately reassigned to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時留都儲峙耗竭，孟男受事，粟僅支二年，不再歲遂有七年之蓄。

translations.literal: At that time Nanjing's stored grain was exhausted; when Mengnan took office grain would last only two years, but within another year there was a seven-year reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's granaries were then nearly empty; when Mengnan took charge the supply would barely cover two years, yet within a year he had built up a seven-year reserve.

sentences.zh: 水衡修倉，發公羨二千金助之。

translations.literal: For the Water Office's granary repairs he disbursed two thousand taels of surplus public funds to assist.
translations.idiomatic: When the Water Office repaired its granaries, he contributed two thousand taels from surplus public funds to help.

sentences.zh: 或謂奈何耘人田，孟男曰：「公家事，乃畫區畔耶？」

translations.literal: Some said why cultivate another man's field; Mengnan said: public affairs — must one draw boundary lines?
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why he was working another man's field, Mengnan replied: if it is the state's business, must one mark off boundaries?

sentences.zh: 南京御史陳所聞劾孟男貪鄙，吏部尚書孫鑨言孟男忠誠謹恪，臺臣所論，事由郎官，帝乃留之。

translations.literal: Nanjing censor Chen Suowen impeached Mengnan as greedy and base; Personnel Minister Sun Rong said Mengnan was loyal, sincere, and careful, and that what the censorate charged arose from a director's office; the emperor then kept him.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing censor Chen Suowen accused Mengnan of greed and meanness, but Personnel Minister Sun Rong testified that Mengnan was loyal and scrupulous and that the censor's charges stemmed from a director's dispute; the emperor kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 孟男求去，不允。

translations.literal: Mengnan requested to leave; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Mengnan asked to resign, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 再疏請，乃聽歸。

translations.literal: He submitted a second memorial requesting leave and was then permitted to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After a second petition to retire, he was at last allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 久之，召拜故官。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned and appointed to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 三十年春，有詔罷礦稅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirtieth year there was an edict abolishing mining taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Wanli 30 an edict announced the abolition of mining levies.

sentences.zh: 已，弗果行。

translations.literal: Soon after, it was not actually carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the order was not put into effect.

sentences.zh: 孟男率同列諫，不報。

translations.literal: Mengnan led his colleagues in remonstrance; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Mengnan led his colleagues in protest, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 加太子少保。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五上章乞歸，不許。

translations.literal: Five times he submitted memorials begging to return home; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned five times to retire, but each request was refused.

sentences.zh: 時礦稅患日劇，孟男草遺疏數千言，極陳其害，言：「臣備員地官，所征天下租稅，皆鬻男市女、朘骨割肉之余也。

translations.literal: At that time the harm of mining taxes grew daily worse; Mengnan drafted a final memorial of several thousand words, stating their evils at length and saying: I hold a place among the territorial officials; all the land tax levied under heaven is what remains after people sell sons and daughters and pare flesh from bone.
translations.idiomatic: As the mining-tax scourge worsened by the day, Mengnan drafted a deathbed memorial thousands of words long, denouncing the levy in detail and declaring: as a territorial official I know that every tax collected across the realm comes from what people have left after selling their children and cutting flesh from their bones.

sentences.zh: 臣以催科為職，臣得其職，而民病矣。

translations.literal: I take tax collection as my duty; I fulfill my duty, yet the people suffer.
translations.idiomatic: My duty is to collect taxes — I perform that duty, and the people are the ones who suffer.

sentences.zh: 聚財以病民，虐民以搖國，有臣如此，安所用之？

translations.literal: Amassing wealth to afflict the people, tyrannizing the people to shake the state — with a minister like this, of what use is he?
translations.idiomatic: To gather riches by harming the people and to oppress the people so as to unsettle the realm — what use is a minister who does this?

sentences.zh: 臣不勝哀鳴，為陛下杞人憂耳。」

translations.literal: I cannot overcome my mournful cry; I am but voicing for Your Majesty the worry of the man of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot contain my grief; I speak only as one who fears for the realm, like the man of Qi who worried that the sky might fall.

sentences.zh: 屬其子上之，明日遂卒。

translations.literal: He had his son submit it; the next day he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had his son present the memorial, and died the following day.

sentences.zh: 南京尚書趙參魯等奏其清忠，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: Nanjing Minister Zhao Canlu and others memorialized his integrity and loyalty; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Minister Zhao Canlu and others praised his upright loyalty, and he was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 衛承芳，字君大，達州人。

translations.literal: Wei Chengfang, courtesy name Junda, was a native of Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chengfang, styled Junda, came from Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing he passed the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Longqing 2.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，累官溫州知府。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he cumulatively served as prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli he rose through the ranks to prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 公廉善撫字。

translations.literal: He was public-spirited and incorrupt, skilled at nurturing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and honest, he was adept at caring for the populace.

sentences.zh: 進浙江副使，謝病歸。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Commissioner in Zhejiang, he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to Vice Commissioner in Zhejiang, he cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 薦起山東參政，歷南京鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Recommended and restored, he became Shandong administrative commissioner and served as Minister of Banquets at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he returned to office, served as Shandong administrative commissioner, and later became Minister of Banquets at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 吏部推太常少卿朱敬循為右通政，以承芳貳之。

translations.literal: Personnel recommended Vice Minister of Ceremonies Zhu Jingxun as Right Commissioner for Transmission, with Chengfang as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel proposed Vice Minister of Ceremonies Zhu Jingxun for Right Commissioner for Transmission, with Chengfang as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 敬循，大學士賡子也。

translations.literal: Jingxun was the son of Grand Secretary Geng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jingxun was the son of Grand Secretary Geng.

sentences.zh: 賡言：「承芳臣同年進士，恬淡之操，世罕能及，臣子不當先。」

translations.literal: Geng said: Chengfang is my fellow jinshi of the same year; his calm, detached integrity the age rarely matches; a minister's son ought not take precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Geng argued: Chengfang was my jinshi year-mate, and his quiet integrity is seldom matched; a minister's son should not rank ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 帝許焉。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋遷南京光祿卿，擢右副都御史，巡撫江西。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Nanjing Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Nanjing Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 嚴絕饋遺，屬吏爭自飭。

translations.literal: He strictly refused gifts; subordinate officials competed to discipline themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He rigorously barred gifts, and his subordinates vied to tighten their own conduct.

sentences.zh: 入為南京兵部右侍郎，就拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He entered as Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing, then was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing, he was immediately appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 福王乞蘆洲，自江都抵太平南北千餘里，自遣內官征課。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu requested reed flats from Jiangdu to Taiping, north and south over a thousand li, dispatching eunuchs himself to collect levies.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu sought reed lands stretching more than a thousand li from Jiangdu to Taiping and sent his own eunuchs to impose levies along the route.

sentences.zh: 承芳抗疏爭，卒不從。

translations.literal: Chengfang submitted forceful memorials in protest; ultimately it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Chengfang protested in strong memorials, but in the end the throne would not yield.

sentences.zh: 萬曆間，南京戶部尚書有清名者，前有張孟男，後則稱承芳。

translations.literal: In Wanli, among Nanjing Revenue ministers with reputations for integrity, before was Zhang Mengnan; afterward Chengfang was so called.
translations.idiomatic: During Wanli, Nanjing ministers of Revenue famed for integrity were first Zhang Mengnan and later Chengfang.

sentences.zh: 尋就改吏部。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was shortly transferred to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still serving.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚清敏。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Qingmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Qingmin.

sentences.zh: 李禎，字維卿，安化人。

translations.literal: Li Zhen, courtesy name Weiqing, was a native of Anhua.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen, styled Weiqing, came from Anhua.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing he passed the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Longqing 5.

sentences.zh: 除高平知縣，征授御史。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Gaoping, he was summoned as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Gaoping before being called up as a censor.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，傅應禎以直言下詔獄，禎與同官喬嚴、給事中徐貞明擁入護視之，坐謫長蘆鹽運司知事。

translations.literal: In the early Wanli reign Fu Yingzhen was imprisoned for blunt speech; Zhen, together with colleague Qiao Yan and supervising secretary Xu Zhenming, forced their way in to guard and visit him, and for this was demoted to clerk of the Changlu Salt Transport Office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli, when Fu Yingzhen was thrown into prison for outspoken remonstrance, Zhen joined colleague Qiao Yan and supervising secretary Xu Zhenming in forcing entry to watch over him and was punished with demotion to clerk of the Changlu Salt Transport Office.

sentences.zh: 遷歸德推官、禮部主事，三遷順天府丞。

translations.literal: Transferred to magistrate's assistant at Guide and director in the Ministry of Rites, he was three times promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to magistrate's assistant at Guide and a directorship in Rites, then rose three times to vice prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 十八年，洮、河有警，極言貢市非策，因歷詆邊吏四失。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year there were alarms on the Tao and Yellow Rivers; he strongly argued that tribute trade was no strategy and sequentially denounced four failures of border officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 18, with trouble on the Tao and Yellow River frontiers, he argued forcefully that tribute trade was no policy and listed four failings of the border administration.

sentences.zh: 帝以納款二十年，不當咎始事，遂寢其議。

translations.literal: The emperor said tribute had been accepted for twenty years and the original policy should not be blamed; the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that tribute relations had stood for twenty years and the original arrangement should not be faulted, so the memorial was set aside.

sentences.zh: 以右僉都御史巡撫湖廣，言：「知縣梁道凝循吏，反註下考，宜懲挾私者以勵其余。

translations.literal: As Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Grand Coordinator of Huguang he said: Magistrate Liang Daoning is a conscientious official yet was marked for the lowest rating; those who judge with private motives should be punished to encourage the rest.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Coordinator of Huguang with the rank of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, he argued that Magistrate Liang Daoning, a capable local administrator, had wrongly received the lowest evaluation and that officials who let bias govern ratings should be punished to spur the others.

sentences.zh: 薦舉屬吏，不應專及高秩，下僚如趙蛟、楊果者，亦當顯旌之。」

translations.literal: In recommending subordinates one should not focus only on high rank; lower officers such as Zhao Jiao and Yang Guo should also be prominently honored.
translations.idiomatic: When recommending staff, one should not single out only senior men; junior officials such as Zhao Jiao and Yang Guo also deserve clear commendation.

sentences.zh: 蛟、果，萬曆初以吏員超擢者也。

translations.literal: Jiao and Guo were men promoted from clerical ranks in the early Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao and Guo were among those raised from clerical posts early in Wanli.

sentences.zh: 詔皆報可。

translations.literal: Edicts approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved each proposal.

sentences.zh: 召為左僉都御史，再遷戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Summoned as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, he was again promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, he was soon advanced to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 趙用賢以絕婚事被訐，戶部郎中鄭材復詆之。

translations.literal: Zhao Yongxian was impeached over breaking off a marriage; Revenue Bureau director Zheng Cai again slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yongxian came under attack for refusing a marriage alliance, Revenue Bureau director Zheng Cai renewed the slander against him.

sentences.zh: 禎駁材疏，語侵其父洛。

translations.literal: Zhen rebutted Cai's memorial; his language impinged on Cai's father Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen answered Cai's memorial in a rebuttal that also touched on Cai's father, Luo.

sentences.zh: 材憤，疏詆禎，禎遂乞休，不允。

translations.literal: Cai was angry and submitted a memorial slandering Zhen; Zhen then begged to retire, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Cai memorialized against Zhen in turn; Zhen asked to retire, but permission was refused.

sentences.zh: 御史宋興祖請改材他部避禎，全大臣體，乃出材南京。

translations.literal: Censor Song Xingzu asked that Cai be transferred to another ministry to avoid Zhen and preserve the dignity of senior ministers; Cai was then sent to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Song Xingzu proposed moving Cai to another ministry so he would not clash with Zhen and the standing of senior ministers would be preserved; Cai was accordingly posted to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 禎尋調兵部，進左侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhen was soon transferred to War and promoted Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was shortly moved to War and raised to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，日本封貢事僨，首輔趙誌臯、尚書石星俱被劾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the Japanese enfeoffment and tribute affair collapsed; Senior Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao and Minister Shi Xing were both impeached.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 24 the Japanese enfeoffment and tribute negotiations broke down, and both Senior Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao and Minister Shi Xing faced impeachment.

sentences.zh: 廷臣議戰守，章悉下兵部。

translations.literal: Court officials debated war and defense; memorials were all sent to War.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated war and defense, and every memorial on the subject went to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 禎等言：「今所議惟戰守封三事。

translations.literal: Zhen and others said: what is now debated are only three matters — war, defense, and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and his colleagues wrote that the debate now turned on only three questions: war, defense, and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 封則李宗城雖征，楊方亨尚在。

translations.literal: As for enfeoffment, although Li Zongcheng was sent on mission, Yang Fangheng is still there.
translations.idiomatic: On enfeoffment, though Li Zongcheng has already been dispatched, Yang Fangheng remains in Japan.

sentences.zh: 若遽議罷，無論中國數百人淪於異域，而我兵食未集，勢難遠征。

translations.literal: If we hastily debate abandoning it, setting aside several hundred Chinese fallen in foreign lands, our troops and supplies are not assembled and a distant expedition would be hard.
translations.idiomatic: To break off the mission abruptly would abandon several hundred countrymen in a foreign land, while our armies and provisions are not yet ready for a distant campaign.

sentences.zh: 宜令方亨靜俟關白來迎則封，不迎則止。

translations.literal: Fangheng should quietly wait: if the kampaku comes to welcome then enfeoff; if not, then stop.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fangheng should wait quietly — if the kampaku comes to receive the envoy, proceed with enfeoffment; if not, halt.

sentences.zh: 我以戰守為實務，而相機應之。

translations.literal: We take war and defense as real business and respond according to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: War and defense should be our substantive work, with policy adjusted as conditions require.

sentences.zh: 且朝鮮素守禮，王師所屯，宜嚴禁擾掠。」

translations.literal: Moreover Korea has always observed propriety; where our armies encamp, plunder should be strictly forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Korea has long upheld ritual decorum, and wherever our troops are stationed they must be strictly barred from looting.

sentences.zh: 得旨如議。

translations.literal: The rescript approved the proposals as submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved the plan as memorialized.

sentences.zh: 而疏內言誌臯、星當去。

translations.literal: Yet within the memorial it stated that Zhigao and Xing ought to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial also held that Zhao Zhigao and Shi Xing should resign.

sentences.zh: 詔詰禎，止令議戰守事，何擅及大臣去留，姑勿問。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Zhen, ordering him to discuss only war and defense matters—why had he on his own authority touched upon the dismissal or retention of senior ministers? For the present he would not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reprimanded Li Zhen: confine yourself to strategy and defense—why did you presume to weigh senior ministers' fate? For now the matter would drop.

sentences.zh: 誌臯自是不悅禎。

translations.literal: From that time Zhigao was displeased with Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhigao thereafter bore a grudge against Li Zhen.

sentences.zh: 明年，星得罪，命禎攝部事。

translations.literal: The following year Xing incurred disgrace, and Zhen was ordered to administer the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shi Xing fell from favor and Li Zhen was told to stand in as minister.

sentences.zh: 禎以平壤、王京、釜山皆朝鮮要地，請修建大城，興屯開鎮，且列上戰守十五策，俱允行。

translations.literal: Zhen held that Pyongyang, Hanseong, and Pusan were all vital places in Korea; he requested building large walled cities, establishing garrison farming and opening military posts, and moreover submitted fifteen policies on war and defense—all approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen urged major fortification, colonization, and new garrisons at Pyongyang, Seoul, and Pusan, Korea's key sites, and laid out fifteen war-and-defense measures—all adopted.

sentences.zh: 後又數上方略。

translations.literal: Later he several times submitted plans to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to send strategic plans to court.

sentences.zh: 四川被寇，禎言：「川、陜接界，而松潘向無寇患者，以諸番為屏蔽也。

translations.literal: When Sichuan suffered raids, Zhen said: "Sichuan and Shaanxi adjoin one another, and Songpan had never suffered raids because the various tribes served as a shield.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan came under attack, Li Zhen argued: "Sichuan borders Shaanxi; Songpan had long been unmolested because tribal peoples formed a buffer.

sentences.zh: 自俺答西牧，隴右騷然。

translations.literal: From the time Altan moved west to pasture, Longyou was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: After Altan drove his herds westward, the Longyou frontier erupted.

sentences.zh: 其後隴右備嚴，寇不得逞，而禍乃移之川矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter Longyou's defenses grew strict, the raiders could not prevail, and disaster shifted to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: As Longyou hardened its defenses the raiders turned aside—and the harm moved into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 今諸番強半折入於西部。

translations.literal: Now more than half the tribes have been broken and absorbed into the western region.
translations.idiomatic: Today more than half the tribes have been subordinated to the western Mongols.

sentences.zh: 臣閱地圖，從北界迤西間道達蜀地，多不隔三舍。

translations.literal: Your servant has studied the maps: from the northern border westward by secret routes to Shu territory, in many places not even three villages intervene.
translations.idiomatic: On the maps, secret routes from the northern frontier into Shu pass through gaps often less than three hamlets apart.

sentences.zh: 幸層巖疊嶂，屹然天險，如鎮虜堡為漳臘門戶，虹橋關為松城咽喉。

translations.literal: Fortunately layered cliffs and overlapping peaks stand as natural barriers—such as Zhenlu Fort guarding the gateway of Zhangla, and Hongqiao Pass the throat of Song prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Only sheer cliffs stand in the way: Zhenlu Fort holds the gate to Zhangla, and Hongqiao Pass guards the neck of Songpan.

sentences.zh: 關堡之外，或嶺或崖，皆可據守。

translations.literal: Beyond the passes and forts, whether ridges or cliff faces, all may be held.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the forts and passes, every ridge and cliff can be garrisoned.

sentences.zh: 守阿玉嶺，則不能越咂際而窺堡。

translations.literal: Hold Ayu Ridge, and they cannot cross Zha Ji and spy on the fort.
translations.idiomatic: Hold Ayu Ridge and the enemy cannot pass Zha Ji to threaten the fort.

sentences.zh: 守黃勝場，則不敢逾塞墩而寇關。

translations.literal: Hold Huang Sheng Field, and they dare not cross the frontier beacons to raid the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Huang Shengchang and they will not dare bypass the beacon towers to strike the pass.

sentences.zh: 他如橫山、寡石崖尤為要害，皆當亟議防禦，令撫鎮臣計畫以聞。」

translations.literal: Others such as Hengshan and Guaishiya are especially critical—all should urgently be discussed for defense; let the provincial and garrison officials plan and report."
translations.idiomatic: Hengshan and Guai Shiya are equally vital—all need urgent defense plans; the governor-generals should draw them up and report.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 禎質直方剛，署事規畫頗當。

translations.literal: Zhen was upright, straightforward, and firm; in acting charge his planning was quite sound.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen was blunt, principled, and firm; his stewardship was judged sound.

sentences.zh: 有欲即用為尚書者，誌臯以故憾，陰沮之。

translations.literal: Some wished to appoint him straightaway as minister, but Zhigao, owing to old resentment, secretly obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged making him minister at once, but Zhao Zhigao, nursing old grievances, quietly blocked it.

sentences.zh: 而張位、沈一貫雅與經略邢玠、經理楊鎬通，亦不便禎所為，言禎非將材，惟蕭大亨堪任。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei and Shen Yiguan were on familiar terms with frontier commander Xing Bing and commissioner Yang Hao, and also found Zhen's conduct inconvenient; they said Zhen was no general's material and only Xiao Dayheng was fit for the post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei and Shen Yiguan, close to Xing Bing and Yang Hao, likewise disliked Li Zhen's course and called him no soldier—only Xiao Dayheng was fit.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 其後玠、鎬益無功，誌臯等又請罷禎，御史況上進劾禎庸鄙。

translations.literal: Later Xing and Yang grew more fruitless; Zhigao and others again asked to dismiss Zhen; Censor Kuang Shangjin impeached Zhen as mediocre and crude.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing and Yang continued to fail, Zhao Zhigao again moved to remove Li Zhen, and Censor Kuang Shangjin charged him with mediocrity.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor heard none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again refused.

sentences.zh: 甘肅缺巡撫，禎以劉敏寬名上。

translations.literal: Gansu lacked a governor; Zhen recommended Liu Minkuan by reputation.
translations.idiomatic: When Gansu needed a governor, Li Zhen nominated the well-known Liu Minkuan.

sentences.zh: 給事楊應文言敏寬方坐事勘，不當推舉。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Yang Yingwen said Minkuan was just then under investigation for an offense and ought not be recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yang Yingwen objected: Liu Minkuan was already under disciplinary review and should not be put forward.

sentences.zh: 帝以詰禎，禎言：「前奉詔，敏寬須巡撫缺用，臣故舉之。」

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon questioned Zhen; Zhen said: "Previously by imperial order Minkuan was to be used when a governorship fell vacant; your servant therefore recommended him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor challenged Li Zhen, who replied: "An earlier edict reserved Liu Minkuan for the next governorship vacancy—that is why I named him.

sentences.zh: 帝怒禎不引罪，調之南京。

translations.literal: The emperor angrily faulted Zhen for not confessing guilt and transferred him to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged that Li Zhen would not admit error, the emperor posted him to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 後考察，南京言官拾遺及禎，遂命致仕。

translations.literal: Later at evaluation the Nanjing censors' supplemental review implicated Zhen, and he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: At the next personnel review Nanjing remonstrators brought charges against him and he was forced to retire.

sentences.zh: 久之，起南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After long service he was recalled as Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was recalled as Nanjing minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 逾年復引疾，不俟報徑歸，帝怒。

translations.literal: After a year he again cited illness, returned home without awaiting approval, and the emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: A year on he pleaded illness again and left for home without waiting for permission; the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 大學士葉向高言：「禎實病，不可深責。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao said: "Zhen is truly ill and should not be severely blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao argued: "Li Zhen is genuinely ill and should not be harshly punished.

sentences.zh: 十余年來，大臣乞休得請者，百無一二。

translations.literal: In more than ten years, of senior ministers begging to retire, scarcely one or two in a hundred were granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: For a decade and more, perhaps one in a hundred senior ministers who asked to retire was allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 李廷機、趙世卿皆羈留數載，疏至百余上。

translations.literal: Li Tingji and Zhao Shiqing were both detained for years, submitting memorials exceeding one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingji and Zhao Shiqing were held at court for years, their pleas numbering over a hundred memorials.

sentences.zh: 今尚書孫丕揚、李化龍又以考察軍政疏不下，相率求去。

translations.literal: Now Ministers Sun Piyang and Li Hualong, because their memorials on military evaluation went unanswered, are leading one another in seeking departure.
translations.idiomatic: Today Ministers Sun Piyang and Li Hualong, whose reviews of military administration have gone unread, are likewise pressing to resign.

sentences.zh: 若復踵禎轍，實傷國體。

translations.literal: If they again follow Zhen's example, it will truly damage the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: If others follow Li Zhen's path, the prestige of the government itself will suffer.

sentences.zh: 諸臣求去，約有數端。

translations.literal: The ministers' requests to leave fall roughly into several categories.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers leave for a handful of reasons.

sentences.zh: 疾病當去，被言當去，不得其職當去。

translations.literal: Illness warrants departure; being impeached warrants departure; inability to fulfill one's office warrants departure.
translations.idiomatic: Sickness, censure, or inability to perform the duties—all are grounds to let a man go.

sentences.zh: 宜曲體其情，可留留之，不可留則聽之。」

translations.literal: Their circumstances should be accommodated with flexibility—keep those who may be kept; where they cannot be kept, let them go."
translations.idiomatic: Meet their circumstances flexibly: keep them when retention is justified, release them when it is not.

sentences.zh: 帝竟奪禎職閑住。

translations.literal: In the end the emperor stripped Zhen of office and ordered him to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nevertheless stripped Li Zhen of rank and ordered him to live in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 丁賓，字禮原，嘉善人。

translations.literal: Ding Bin, styled Liyuan, was a native of Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Bin, courtesy name Liyuan, came from Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in Longqing 5.

sentences.zh: 授句容知縣。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 征授御史。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was called up and made a censor.

sentences.zh: 大學士張居正，賓座主也，誣劉臺以贓，屬賓往遼東按之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng, Bin's examination patron, falsely charged Liu Tai with corruption and assigned Bin to go to Liaodong to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng—Bin's examiner—framed Liu Tai for graft and sent Bin to Liaodong to prosecute the case.

sentences.zh: 賓力辭，忤居正意，去官。

translations.literal: Bin forcefully declined, offending Juzheng's intent, and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Bin refused outright, provoked Juzheng, and resigned.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十九年，用薦起故官，復以憂去。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Wanli, on recommendation he was restored to his former rank, but again left on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 19 brought restoration on recommendation, but mourning soon took him home again.

sentences.zh: 起南京大理丞。

translations.literal: Recalled as assistant director of the Nanjing Court of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as assistant director of the Nanjing Court of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京右僉都御史兼督操江。

translations.literal: He rose through promotions to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing, concurrently supervising the Yangtze patrol.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Nanjing Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and inspector of Yangtze river defenses.

sentences.zh: 江防多懈，賓率將校乘一舟往來周視，增守兵戍要害，部內宴然。

translations.literal: River defense was largely lax; Bin led officers in a single boat back and forth on inspection, increased garrison troops at critical points, and within his jurisdiction all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: With river defenses slack, he toured the line in one boat with his officers, reinforced critical posts, and kept his jurisdiction at peace.

sentences.zh: 南衛世職率赴京師請襲，留滯不得官，賓請就南勘襲。

translations.literal: Hereditary officers of the southern garrison generally went to the capital to request succession, lingering without appointment; Bin asked that inspection for succession be carried out in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Southern garrison officers who traveled to the capital to claim hereditary posts often languished without appointment; he proposed conducting succession reviews in Nanjing instead.

sentences.zh: 妖民劉天緒左道事覺，兵部尚書孫钅廣欲窮治之，詔下法司訊鞫。

translations.literal: The heterodox affair of sorcerer Liu Tianxu was exposed; Minister of War Sun Kuang wished to pursue it to the end; an edict sent the case to the judiciary for trial.
translations.idiomatic: When the heretical cult of Liu Tianxu was exposed, War Minister Sun Kuang sought a sweeping prosecution; the court referred the case to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 賓兼攝刑部大理事，力平反，論七人死，余皆獲釋。

translations.literal: Bin concurrently handled the Nanjing Ministry of Justice grand review; he forcefully reversed the verdicts—seven condemned to death, the rest all released.
translations.idiomatic: Acting as Nanjing chief judicial reviewer, he overturned the case: seven were sentenced to death, the rest freed.

sentences.zh: 召拜工部左侍郎，尋擢南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Left Vice Minister of Works, soon promoted to Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to be Left Vice Minister of Works and soon made Nanjing minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 自上元至丹陽道路，盡易以石，行旅頌之。

translations.literal: The road from Shangyuan to Danyang was entirely repaved in stone, and travelers praised it.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced the road from Nanjing proper to Danyang with stone paving, to travelers' acclaim.

sentences.zh: 數引年乞罷，光宗立，始予致仕。

translations.literal: Several times citing old age he begged dismissal; when Guangzong ascended, he was at last granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire on grounds of age; only when Guangzong took the throne was release granted.

sentences.zh: 賓官南都三十年，每遇旱潦，輒請振貸，時出家財佐之。

translations.literal: Bin served at the Southern Capital for thirty years; whenever drought or flood occurred he requested relief loans, sometimes supplementing with his own family wealth.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years in Nanjing office he sought famine relief whenever drought or flood struck, often adding his own funds.

sentences.zh: 初以御史家居，及丁憂歸，連三年大饑，鹹捐資以振。

translations.literal: When he first lived at home as a censor, and later returned on mourning leave, three years of great famine followed in succession; all contributed funds for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in retirement as a censor, then again during mourning leave, three consecutive famine years led him to give generously for relief.

sentences.zh: 至天啟五年，復捐粟三千石振貧民，以資三千金代下戶之不能輸賦者。

translations.literal: By the fifth year of Tianqi, he again donated three thousand shi of grain to relieve the poor, and three thousand taels to cover taxes for lower households unable to pay.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 5 he again gave three thousand shi of grain to the poor and three thousand taels to pay taxes for impoverished households.

sentences.zh: 撫按錄上其先後事，時已加太子少保，詔進太子太保，旌其門。

translations.literal: Governor and censor recorded and forwarded his successive deeds; he had already been given Junior Guard of the Heir Apparent; an edict promoted him to Senior Guard of the Heir Apparent and honored his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial authorities reported his record of charity; already a Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, he was raised to Senior Guardian and his household was publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 以年高，三被存問。

translations.literal: Owing to advanced age, three times he was visited with imperial concern.
translations.idiomatic: In his great age he received three imperial inquiries after his welfare.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年卒，年九十一。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongzhen he died, aged ninety-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chongzhen 6 at the age of ninety-one.

sentences.zh: 謚清惠。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Qinghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Qinghui ("Pure and Kind").

sentences.zh: 贊曰：南京卿長，體貌尊而官守無責，故為養望之地，資地深而譽聞重者處焉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Senior ministers at Nanjing enjoy honored stature yet bear no governing responsibility, and so it is a place for cultivating reputation; men of profound standing and weighty renown are stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: The historians note: Nanjing ministries were posts of high dignity but little executive weight—a garden in which to cultivate standing; men of depth and reputation were sent there.

sentences.zh: 或強直無所附麗，不為執政所喜，則以此遠之。

translations.literal: Some, being upright and attached to no faction, not favored by those in power, were for that reason distanced thus.
translations.idiomatic: Those who were stern and independent, and therefore disliked by the men in power, were kept at such a distance.

sentences.zh: 袁洪愈諸人類以清強居優閑之地，不竟其用，亦以自全。

translations.literal: Yuan Hongyu and men like him, by virtue of integrity and firmness dwelling in leisurely posts, did not exhaust their use—and also preserved themselves thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yuan Hongyu lived out their careers in these honorable but idle posts, their talents unused—yet preserving themselves in the process.

sentences.zh: 幹時冒進之徒，可以風矣。

translations.literal: Those who in their time rush forward recklessly may take this as a lesson.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious climbers of the age might take the lesson to heart.
